**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 9, Verses 1–4**

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Bara'ah* (براءة): That is, this is a disavowal (*bara'ah*), meaning a repudiation, a distancing, and a release.

*'Ahadtum* (عاهدتم): That is, you made between yourselves and them a covenant (*'ahd*) and a pact (*mithaq*).

*Fa-sihu fi al-ard* (فسيحوا في الأرض): That is, travel through the land seeking your own safety.

*Mukhzi al-kafirin* (مخزي الكافرين): Humiliating the disbelievers and degrading them.

*Wa-adhan min Allah* (وأذان من الله): A proclamation (*i'lam*) from Him, exalted is He.

*Yawm al-hajj al-akbar* (يوم الحج الأكبر): That is, the Day of the Sacrifice (*'Id al-Nahr*).

*Lam yanqusukum shay'an* (لم ينقصوكم شيئاً): That is, they did not fall short of you in any of the conditions of the treaty or the clauses of the agreement.

*Wa-lam yuzahiru 'alaykum ahadan* (ولم يظاهروا عليكم أحداً): That is, they did not assist anyone against you.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

This is the only surah of the Qur'an that lacks the *basmalah*, because it opens with verses of punishment, and the mention of mercy would be incongruous with them. This surah is among the last of the surahs of the Noble Qur'an revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Ali and some of the Companions during the Hajj of the year nine (AH) to recite these verses at the gathering (*mawsim*). They inform the polytheists that whoever has an unrestricted covenant without a fixed term, such as a month or a year, or has a covenant of less than four months, or has a covenant of more than four months and has violated it, [the following applies]: you are to travel through the land under complete safety for a period of four months. If they embrace Islam, that is better for them. If they leave the Arabian Peninsula, they may do so. If they remain disbelievers, they will be seized and killed wherever they are found in the lands of the Peninsula, which had become a land of Islam through the conquest of Makkah and the entry of the people of al-Ta'if into Islam. This is the meaning of His statement, ﴿A disavowal from Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, reaching ﴿those with whom you made covenants among the polytheists. So travel freely through the land for four months﴾, beginning from the day of this announcement, which is the Day of the Sacrifice (*'Id al-Adha*).

His statement, ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, means you cannot outrun Him or flee from His subjugation and authority over you. This is first. Second, ﴿and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, that is, He will humiliate them.

His statement, ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). The *adhan* means announcement and notification. ﴿To the people﴾, who are the polytheists. ﴿On the day of the greater Hajj﴾, that is, the Day of the Sacrifice, when the pilgrims are free to stay in Mina for rest and relaxation before returning to their homes. The form of the announcement of that disavowal is His statement, ﴿That Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾, that is, likewise He is free of the polytheists and of His obligation toward them. ﴿So if you repent﴾, O polytheists, turning to Allah in repentance by affirming His oneness, believing in His Messenger, and obeying Him and His Messenger, ﴿it is better for you﴾ than persisting in polytheism, disbelief, and disobedience. ﴿But if you turn away﴾, that is, you refuse faith and obedience, ﴿then know that you cannot escape Allah﴾ in any circumstance; you will never elude Him, nor will you escape His authority, for Allah is not overcome by any conqueror, nor does any fugitive elude Him.

Then Allah said to His Messenger, ﴿And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾, that is, inform them of it, for it will befall them without doubt unless they repent.

As for His statement in the fourth verse [4], ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists, who have not fallen short of you in any of the conditions of the treaty﴾, ﴿and have not assisted anyone against you﴾, that is, they did not support anyone against you, neither with men, nor with weapons, nor even with counsel and opinion. These are the ones from whom Allah and His Messenger have not disavowed themselves. Accordingly, ﴿fulfill for them their covenant until their term﴾, that is, the period of their specified time. So keep your promises to them and do not violate a covenant with them until they violate it themselves, or until their term ends. At that point, it will be either Islam or the sword, since there is no longer room for polytheism to remain within the abode of Islam and its dome.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The permissibility of concluding treaties between Muslims and disbelievers when this serves to repel a certain harm from the Muslims, or to bring about a certain benefit to Islam and the Muslims.

2. The prohibition of treachery and betrayal. Therefore, the cancellation of treaties was to be announced publicly, and their holders were given a period of four months to consider their situation and seek what is best for them.

3. The obligation to fulfill treaties with fixed terms until their term expires, unless the signatories themselves violate them.

4. The virtue of piety (*taqwa*) and its people, which is guarding against the displeasure of Allah by doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 5–8:

Explanation of the words:

"Fa-idha insalakha al-ashhur al-hurum" (so when the sacred months have passed): they have ended and the four months in which you granted the polytheists safe conduct have gone out.

"Haythu wajadtumuhum" (wherever you find them): that is, in whatever place you meet them, whether within the sacred territory (al-hill) or within the Sacred Precinct (al-haram).

"Wa-khudhuhum" (and seize them): that is, as captives.

"Wa-ahsuruhum" (and besiege them): that is, lay siege to them until they surrender themselves.

"Wa-q'udu lahum kulla marsad" (and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush): that is, sit in wait for them on their roads and watch their movements.

"Fa-in tabu" (but if they repent): that is, they believe in Allah and His Messenger.

"Fa-khalluu sabilahum" (then let them go their way): that is, leave them alone, with no siege, no pursuit, and no fighting.

"Istajarak" (seeks your protection): that is, asks you for your protection, i.e., your safeguarding.

"Ma'manahu" (his place of safety): that is, the place where he is secure.

"Fa-ma istaqamu lakum" (so long as they remain true to you): that is, they have not broken their covenant nor violated the agreement.

"Wa-in yazhharu 'alaykum" (and if they gain the upper hand over you): that is, they overcome you.

"La yarqubu fikum" (they do not observe toward you): that is, they do not respect or honour you.

"Illa wa-la dhimmatan" (neither ties of kinship nor covenant): that is, neither kinship nor covenant. Al-il means kinship, and al-dhimma means covenant.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the declaration of a general war against the polytheists, to cleanse the land of the Arabian Peninsula, which is the abode and domain of Islam, from the remnants of polytheism and the polytheists. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger and the believers: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, that is, when the sacred months in which you granted the polytheists safe conduct have ended and passed, those who have no covenant, or who have a covenant but for less than four months or more than four months and without a fixed limit. ﴿And seize them﴾ as captives, ﴿and besiege them﴾ until they surrender, ﴿and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, that is, block their roads against them until they present themselves as Muslims or as those who submit. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿But if they repent﴾, that is, from polytheism and from fighting you, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go their way﴾, since they have become Muslims like you. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means that Allah will forgive them and show them mercy after their Islam, because He, the Exalted, is Forgiving and Merciful. This is what the first verse [5] indicates. As for the second verse [6], Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to grant protection to any polytheist who asks for his protection, until he hears the words of Allah from him (ﷺ) and comprehends the call of Islam. Then he is free to choose: if he wishes, he becomes Muslim, which is better for him; and if he does not become Muslim, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returns him to a place where he is safe from the Muslims who might kill him.

This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah; then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.﴾ Therefore, what they asked of protection was accepted from them until they hear the words of Allah, the Exalted, for if they knew, they would not have turned away from monotheism to polytheism. As for His saying, the Exalted, in the third verse [7]: ﴿How can there be for the polytheists a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger?﴾ This interrogation carries negation along with astonishment, meaning that they have no covenant at all, for they are disbelievers and treacherous. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram. So as long as they remain true to you, be true to them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾ These were some of the Banu Bakr ibn Kinanah, with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant in the year of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, and they were near the Sacred Precinct. These people have a covenant and protection as long as they remain faithful to their covenant and do not break it.

So if they remain true, the Muslims must also remain true to them and not kill them, fulfilling their covenant and out of piety toward Allah the Exalted, because He, the Exalted, dislikes treachery and loves the righteous for that reason. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿How [can there be a covenant], while if they gain the upper hand over you, they would not observe toward you any ties of kinship or covenant?﴾ The interrogation is one of astonishment, meaning how could the polytheists have a covenant that they would keep with you when, if they gain the upper hand over you in battle, ﴿they would not observe toward you﴾, that is, they would not respect Allah, nor kinship, nor covenant, but would kill you with a devastating slaughter. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They satisfy you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ is an announcement from Allah the Exalted about those polytheists who break covenants and are treacherous, that they try to please the believers with falsehood by their mouths, while their disbelieving hearts refuse what they say with their tongues, that is, they do not believe in it or affirm it. ﴿And most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾, who know neither obedience nor commitment, neither to a covenant nor to a religion. The passage contains an incitement of the Muslims to fight the polytheists, to besiege and seize them, to cleanse the land of the Arabian Peninsula of them before the death of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to fulfil covenants, so long as the covenanted parties do not break them.

2- Establishing the principle of firmness in fighting and striking with severity.

3- The obligation to cleanse the Arabian Peninsula of all polytheism and disbelief, because it is the abode of Islam.

4- Establishing prayer is a condition for the validity of faith, so whoever abandons it is a disbeliever and not a believer.

5- Respect for protection (jiwar), and its acknowledgment, and securing envoys and representatives of a disbelieving state.

6- Accepting the request of anyone among the disbelievers who asks permission to enter the lands of Islam in order to learn the Islamic religion.

7- The Qur'an is truly the speech of Allah the Exalted, in both its letters and its meanings, as indicated by ﴿until he hears the words of Allah﴾, which is recited to him (ﷺ).

8- The obligation to be mindful of Allah the Exalted, to observe ties of kinship, and to respect covenants.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 9–12:

Explanation of the words:

"Ishtarawu bi-ayati Allah" (they have exchanged the signs of God): i.e., they sold the signs of God and took in exchange disbelief (kufr).

"Fa-sadda 'an sabilihi" (and so they barred from His way): i.e., they turned away from the way of God, which is Islam, and likewise barred others as well.

"Saa'" (evil is): i.e., it is ugly.

"La yarqubun" (they do not observe): i.e., they do not respect.

"Illan" (a bond of kinship): al-Il means God, and it also means kinship and covenant; all of these are suitable here.

"Fa-in taabu" (but if they repent): i.e., from polytheism and hostility.

"Nakathu" (they broke): i.e., they violated and betrayed.

"Wa-ta'anu fi dinikum" (and they attacked your religion): i.e., they criticized Islam in its beliefs, its acts of worship, or its dealings.

"A'immat al-kufr" (leaders of disbelief): i.e., the chiefs of disbelief who are followed and imitated in polytheism, evil, and corruption.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues speaking about the polytheists and explaining what must be done regarding them. God, exalted is He, informs about them in His words in verse [9]: ﴿They have exchanged the signs of God for a small price﴾, meaning they sold faith for disbelief, and so they barred themselves, as well as those who follow them, from Islam, which is the method of their life and the path to their happiness and perfection. Therefore God said, condemning their conduct: ﴿Evil is what they used to do﴾. He also informed that they do not observe, regarding any believer whom they have power over, God (may He be mighty and majestic) or any kinship or covenant that binds them with his people, so He said: ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any bond of kinship or covenant, and it is those who are the transgressors﴾. His description of them as transgressors indicates that they do not respect covenants and do not fear God in anything, owing to the darkness of their souls resulting from disbelief and disobedience. Therefore it is incumbent upon the Muslims to kill them wherever they find them, to take them captive, to besiege them, and to cut off the roads to them until they lay down their weapons and submit to God, or surrender to the believers. The exception is if they repent by faith and entering Islam, as God said: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion﴾. And His words ﴿We detail the signs for a people who know﴾ mean: We make clear the Qur'anic verses containing the proofs and evidences of the oneness of God, the affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the legal rulings concerning war and peace, as in this context. His words ﴿for a people who know﴾ are because those among the ignorant who do not know do not benefit from them, due to the darkness of their souls and the corruption of their minds by the misguidance of polytheism and whims.

In the fourth verse [12], God says: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion﴾. He means those treaty-bound polytheists who, having broken their oaths by which they had confirmed their covenants, undid what they had established and violated what they had firmly bound of pact and agreement, and who reviled Islam and attacked it. They are therefore leaders of disbelief and chiefs of the disbelievers. So fight them without leniency, and do not regard any oaths they swear to you, for they have no oaths. Fight them in hope that they will desist from disbelief, treachery, and betrayal, so that they will affirm the oneness of God, submit, and become, like you, friends of God rather than His enemies.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Censure of the conduct of the disbelievers and their behavior in life; it suffices that they sold truth for falsehood and purchased misguidance in exchange for guidance.

2- One whose character is transgression cannot be trusted with anything and cannot be relied upon in anything, because of the corruption of his psychological disposition.

3- The brotherhood of Islam is established by three matters: monotheism, establishing prayer, and giving zakah.

4- Attacking the religion is apostasy and disbelief that warrants killing and fighting.

Explanation of the words:

Alā: an interjection of urging (taḥḍīḍ).

Nakathū aymānahum: they broke their oaths, undid them, and did not abide by them.

Hammū bi-ikhrāj al-Rasūl: from the Dār al-Nadwa (the council house of Quraysh), when they resolved on one of three things: imprisonment, exile, or killing.

Awwala marra: that is, at Badr, or at Mā' al-Hayjā', where Quraysh aided Banū Bakr against Khuzā'a.

Wa-yukhzihim: that is, He humiliates and disgraces them.

Wa-yashfi ṣudūra: that is, He removes the rage that was in their hearts against the wrongdoing polytheists.

The meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning the polytheists and the measures that must be taken regarding them. After He had given them the stated period, four months, granting them safety during it, and that period has now expired, nothing remains but fighting them, seizing them, and ending the league of polytheists and its traces in the lands of God. So God, the Exalted, addresses the believers, stirring them up, saying: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths﴾. This is one sin, sufficient to make fighting them obligatory. The second is their plotting to expel the Messenger from among them, from Makkah. The third is that they began the fighting against you at Badr, when their caravan was saved, yet they refused except to fight you. So why do you not fight them? Do you leave off fighting them out of fear and dread of them, if this is the case? ﴿God has more right that you should fear Him, if you are believers﴾, because what God possesses of punishment is not possessed by the polytheists, so God is more worthy of being feared. This is what the first verse [13] contains, namely His saying: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths, and plotted to expel the Messenger, and they began against you the first time? Do you fear them? God has more right that you should fear Him, if you are believers.﴾

In the second verse [14], God says: ﴿Fight them﴾, which is a clear command to fight, and He mentions the reward that follows from fighting them, saying: ﴿God will punish them at your hands, and will disgrace them, and give you victory over them, and will heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, namely the Khuzā'a, whose hearts would be healed of their rage against Banū Bakr, who fought them, and whom Quraysh aided against them after the treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyya. His saying, ﴿And God relents toward whom He wills﴾, is not, though it is among the four [consequences] mentioned before it, a reward for the command to fight. Rather, it is God's custom that when people see their enemies triumph over them in every battle, they incline toward them and accept their religion and the qualities they hold. So the fighting of the believers against the disbelievers and their victory over them opens the opportunity for many disbelievers to embrace Islam, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And God relents toward whom He wills﴾. His saying ﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ affirms the command to fight and the good results that follow from it, the last of which is that God relents toward whom He wills.

As for His saying in the last verse [16]: ﴿Or do you think that you will be left [alone]﴾, that is, without being tested. Among the things the hypocrites used to whisper was discouragement from fighting, on the pretext that Makkah had been conquered and Islam had become mighty, so there was no need to pursue the remnants of the polytheists. Yet they knew that there were alliances led by those discontented with Islam, including some of the notables of Quraysh, who wished to pounce upon the Muslims and nullify every victory that had been achieved for them. This meaning is evident from the context of the verse: ﴿Or do you think that you will be left [alone] while God has not yet known those of you who strove and did not take, besides God and His Messenger and the believers, any intimate confidant﴾, for there are those who took, besides God and His Messenger and the believers, intimate confidants whom they let in on the affairs of the Muslims, concealing matters from them while being among them as insiders. This sentence with which the verse concludes confirms it, namely His saying: ﴿And God is All-Aware of what you do﴾.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 17–18:

Explanation of the words:

"ما كان للمشركين" (It is not for the polytheists): meaning, it is not their place or within their capacity.

"حبطت أعمالهم" (Their deeds are rendered void): meaning, they are nullified, so they are not rewarded for them and do not succeed in them.

"يعمروا مساجد الله" (Maintain the mosques of God): meaning, by worshipping in them, and by preserving and purifying them.

"ولم يخش إلا الله" (And fear none but God): meaning, he does not fear anyone other than God, the Exalted.

"فعسى" (Perhaps): the "عسى" (perhaps) from God, the Exalted, as it is here, conveys certainty, meaning their guidance is assured.

"المهتدين" (the guided): meaning, to the path of salvation from loss and the attainment of the Gardens.

The meaning of the two verses:

There is no doubt that among the polytheists there were those who claimed that they maintained the Sacred Mosque through the custodianship (al-sidana), the keeping of its keys (al-hijaba), and the provision of water (al-siqaya), whether the one making this claim was al-Abbas on the day of Badr or someone else. God, the Exalted, nullified this claim and said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God﴾, meaning it is not fitting for them, nor is it valid from them. And how could it be, when they are disbelievers who bear witness against themselves to their disbelief? Does one who disbelieves in God maintain His house, and by what would he maintain it? When you ask the Jew, "What are you?" he says, "A Jew"; when you ask the Christian, "What are you?" he says, "A Christian"; and when you ask the idolater, "What are you?" he says, "A polytheist." This is their testimony against themselves of disbelief. And His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Those are the ones﴾, meaning the far-removed in disbelief and error, ﴿whose deeds have become void﴾, meaning they have been nullified and lost because they lack sincerity toward God, the Exalted, ﴿and in the Fire they will abide forever﴾, not leaving it at any time once they enter it, since they have no deed that would intercede for them to leave it. Then God, the Exalted, established the truth, which is that those who truly and sincerely maintain the mosques of God are the believers, the monotheists, who establish the prayer, give the zakat, and fear God alone and fear none other than Him. These are the ones worthy of maintaining the mosques through prayer, remembrance, and learning the religious sciences within them, in addition to building, purifying, and preserving them. These are the ones deserving of guidance to every perfection and good, as His saying, the Exalted, testifies: ﴿Perhaps those will be among the guided﴾, to what is the truth and the right, and to the path of salvation from the Fire and the triumph of Paradise.

Lessons of the two verses:

Among the lessons of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of a disbeliever entering the mosques, except out of necessity and with permission from the Muslims.

2- The virtue of maintaining the mosques through worship in them, purifying them, and preserving them.

3- The excellence and nobility of the Muslim, for whoever is asked about his religion answers with a reply that is disbelief, except the Muslim, who says, "Muslim," meaning submitted to God. He is thus the believer, and everyone else is a disbeliever.

4- The obligation of belief in God and the Last Day, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, and fear of God, the Exalted.

5- The people of security and salvation from the Fire are the possessors of the four qualities mentioned in the verse.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 17–18:

Explanation of the words:

"ما كان للمشركين" (It is not for the polytheists): meaning, it is not their place or within their capacity.

"حبطت أعمالهم" (Their deeds are rendered void): meaning, they are nullified, so they are not rewarded for them and do not succeed in them.

"يعمروا مساجد الله" (Maintain the mosques of God): meaning, by worshipping in them, and by preserving and purifying them.

"ولم يخش إلا الله" (And fear none but God): meaning, he does not fear anyone other than God, the Exalted.

"فعسى" (Perhaps): the "عسى" (perhaps) from God, the Exalted, as it is here, conveys certainty, meaning their guidance is assured.

"المهتدين" (the guided): meaning, to the path of salvation from loss and the attainment of the Gardens.

The meaning of the two verses:

There is no doubt that among the polytheists there were those who claimed that they maintained the Sacred Mosque through the custodianship (al-sidana), the keeping of its keys (al-hijaba), and the provision of water (al-siqaya), whether the one making this claim was al-Abbas on the day of Badr or someone else. God, the Exalted, nullified this claim and said: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God﴾, meaning it is not fitting for them, nor is it valid from them. And how could it be, when they are disbelievers who bear witness against themselves to their disbelief? Does one who disbelieves in God maintain His house, and by what would he maintain it? When you ask the Jew, "What are you?" he says, "A Jew"; when you ask the Christian, "What are you?" he says, "A Christian"; and when you ask the idolater, "What are you?" he says, "A polytheist." This is their testimony against themselves of disbelief. And His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Those are the ones﴾, meaning the far-removed in disbelief and error, ﴿whose deeds have become void﴾, meaning they have been nullified and lost because they lack sincerity toward God, the Exalted, ﴿and in the Fire they will abide forever﴾, not leaving it at any time once they enter it, since they have no deed that would intercede for them to leave it. Then God, the Exalted, established the truth, which is that those who truly and sincerely maintain the mosques of God are the believers, the monotheists, who establish the prayer, give the zakat, and fear God alone and fear none other than Him. These are the ones worthy of maintaining the mosques through prayer, remembrance, and learning the religious sciences within them, in addition to building, purifying, and preserving them. These are the ones deserving of guidance to every perfection and good, as His saying, the Exalted, testifies: ﴿Perhaps those will be among the guided﴾, to what is the truth and the right, and to the path of salvation from the Fire and the triumph of Paradise.

1- The prohibition of a disbeliever entering the mosques, except out of necessity and with permission from the Muslims.

2- The virtue of maintaining the mosques through worship in them, purifying them, and preserving them.

3- The excellence and nobility of the Muslim, for whoever is asked about his religion answers with a reply that is disbelief, except the Muslim, who says, "Muslim," meaning submitted to God. He is thus the believer, and everyone else is a disbeliever.

4- The obligation of belief in God and the Last Day, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, and fear of God, the Exalted.

5- The people of security and salvation from the Fire are the possessors of the four qualities mentioned in the verse.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 19–22:

Explanation of the words:

Siqayat al-hajj (the watering of the pilgrims): a place in the Sacred Mosque where water is placed and given to the pilgrims free of charge.

Wa-'imarat al-Masjid al-Haram (and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque): here it refers to its construction, its upkeep, and the custody of the House within it.

La yastawun 'inda Allah (they are not equal in the sight of God): since the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque alongside shirk and disbelief is not worth anything.

Wa-Allahu la yahdi al-qawm al-zalimin (and God does not guide the wrongdoing people): that is, the polytheists, He does not guide them to what would perfect them and bring them happiness.

Ridwan (good pleasure): that is, the pleasure of God, Mighty and Majestic, with them.

Na'im muqim (lasting bliss): that is, enduring, never ceasing or ending.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still continues in refutation of those who viewed the honouring of the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque through the watering, the keeping of its key, and the custody of the House as superior to faith, emigration, and jihad. So God, Exalted, rebuked them, saying: ﴿Do you consider the watering of the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God?﴾ They are ﴿not equal﴾ in the judgment and decree of God under any circumstances. The polytheists are wrongdoers; how could their maintenance of the Sacred Mosque have any weight or value worth mentioning? ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ After this rebuke and clarification of the situation, God informed that ﴿those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of God with their wealth and their lives﴾ are ﴿greater in rank﴾ than those who believed but did not complete these four attributes. He informed that they are the ones who achieve salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise. Greater than this is what came in His saying: ﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him﴾, which is Paradise, ﴿and good pleasure﴾ from Him, which is the greatest bliss, ﴿and gardens﴾, that is, orchards in the Highest Dominion, ﴿for them therein is lasting bliss﴾, which does not change or vanish; and that they will abide therein forever, never leaving it. ﴿Indeed, with God is a great reward﴾ whose worth cannot be measured. May God make us among them and gather us in their company.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The most complete of the believers and the highest in rank, and the closest to God in station, are those who combined the three attributes mentioned in verse [20], namely faith, emigration, and jihad in the way of God with wealth and self.

2- The virtue of emigration and jihad.

3- The variation among the people of Paradise in the loftiness of their ranks.

4- The deprivation of wrongdoers who are deeply immersed in wrongdoing from God's guidance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 23–24:

Explanation of the words:

Awliya' (protectors, allies): plural of waliyy, the one whom you take as a friend through love and support, and who takes you as a friend in the same way.

Istahabbu (they prefer): that is, they loved disbelief over faith.

Al-zalimun (the wrongdoers): zulm (wrongdoing) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. Whoever loves one whose love is not permissible has placed something in other than its place, and so is a wrongdoer.

Wa-'ashiratukum (your kinsfolk): that is, your relatives by lineage, such as distant paternal uncles and their sons.

Iqtaraftumuha (you have earned them): that is, you have acquired them.

Kasadaha (its slackness): its ruin and lack of demand.

Fatarabbasu (then wait): that is, await.

Hatta ya'tiya Allahu bi-amrihi (until Allah brings His command): that is, the punishment for this disobedience on the day of the conquest of Makkah.

Meaning of the two verses:

This is a warning from Allah the Exalted to the believers, forbidding them to take as protectors those of their fathers and brothers who disbelieve, people with whom they would show affection, give support, and reveal to them the secrets and inner affairs of the Muslims. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, in Allah, His Messenger, the meeting with Allah, and His promise and threat, ﴿do not take your fathers and your brothers as protectors if they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, that is, they prioritize disbelief and persistence in it over belief in Allah and His Messenger. Then He threatens them if they do not comply with His command and sever ties with their fathers and brothers who prefer disbelief over faith, saying: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies - then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾. The nature of the wrongdoing is clear: they placed love where hatred belongs, and support where abandonment belongs. Zulm is placing a thing in other than its proper place. Then Allah commanded His Messenger to say to them - and this turning away from addressing them directly to an intermediary conveys anger, displeasure, threat and warning: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have earned, the commerce whose slackness you fear, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause﴾, and so you abandon emigration and jihad for their sake, ﴿then wait until Allah brings His command﴾, that is, await the command of Allah, which is the conquest of Makkah over you and the sending down of punishment upon you. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, that is, He does not grant them success on the path of their salvation and happiness.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The prohibition of taking disbelievers as allies whom one shows affection to, even if they are among the closest relatives, such as a father, son or brother.

2- Taking as allies those who oppose Allah, His Messenger and the believers is a grievous wrong.

3- The obligation to love Allah and His Messenger and to strive in His cause, and to love all that Allah loves and to hate all that Allah hates, in beliefs, states, deeds, persons and attributes.

4- Those who are deeply immersed in defiance are deprived of Allah's guidance to what would perfect and bring them happiness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 25–28:

Explanation of the words:

Fi mawatin (في مواطن): "mawatin" is the plural of "mawtin," meaning a homeland, i.e., the place where a person resides.

Hunayn (حنين): a valley a short distance from al-Ta'if.

Idh a'jabatkum kathratukum (إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم): that is, the abundance of your numbers, to the point that some said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers."

Fa lam tughni 'ankum shay'an (فلم تغن عنكم شيئاً): that is, it did not avail you anything of any benefit when you were routed at the outset of the encounter.

Wa daqat 'alaykumu al-ard (وضاقت عليكم الأرض): that is, you did not know where to go or how to act, as if you were confined to a narrow place.

Bima rahubat (بما رحبت): that is, despite its breadth and vastness.

Anzala Allahu sakinatahu (أنزل الله سكينته): that is, tranquility in their souls, so that anxiety and agitation departed.

Wa anzala junudan (وأنزل جنوداً): that is, of the angels.

Najas (نجس): that is, possessors of impurity, due to the corruption of their souls through shirk.

Ba'da 'amihim hadha (بعد عامهم هذا): the year nine after the Hijra.

'Aylah (عيلة): that is, poverty, destitution, and need.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah forbade the believers to take disbelievers as allies, even if they were their relatives, and warned them against holding back from emigration and jihad—and since what usually kept a person from this was cowardice and fear—He informed them in these three verses that He is their helper and supporter, so that cowardice and fear should not keep them from fulfilling the duty of emigration and jihad. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has given you victory in many battlefields﴾ such as Badr, al-Nadir, Qurayzah, the Conquest, and others, ﴿and on the day of Hunayn﴾ when they fought the tribe of Hawazin, reminding them of a defeat that befell the believers as a result of an error by some of them, namely being deluded by the abundance of their numbers, when some of them said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." They were twelve thousand, while their enemy was only four thousand. As soon as they penetrated between the sides of the valley, the enemy rained upon them a torrent of arrows and javelins, and they did not know how to act, until the earth became narrow for them despite its breadth, and they turned back fleeing in retreat. None remained firm except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was on his white mule called "al-Duldul," with al-'Abbas at his side and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, his cousin. Then the caller of the Messenger of Allah called out: "O companions of Surat al-Baqarah, come! O companions of the tree (the tree of the Pledge of al-Ridwan), come!" So they returned to the battle, and its wheel turned. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts﴾ which touched the hearts and breathed into them the spirit of courage, patience, and steadfastness. So they persevered and fought, and within an hour the enemy was taken captive before them. Never had they gained booty like what they gained that day, for the number of camels reached twelve thousand camels, and of sheep there was an uncountable and unnumbered amount. Thus came His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great numbers pleased you but they availed you nothing, and the earth was confined for you despite its vastness, then you turned back fleeing﴾ that is, fleeing from the enemy. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts﴾ that is, of angels ﴿which you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved﴾ that is, Hawazin. ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, that is, the killing and captivity.

As for His saying: ﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills﴾ that is, after your fighting against the disbelievers and your killing of those you killed, Allah relents to whomever He wills of those who remained alive after the battle. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ He forgives those among the polytheists whom He accepts in repentance their past sins of shirk and all other sins, and shows them mercy by admitting them to Paradise along with whomever He wills of the believers who are sincere in their faith. This is what the three verses indicate. As for the fourth verse: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are impure, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ He, the Exalted, commanded the believers to prevent every polytheist man and woman from entering al-Masjid al-Haram, because the polytheist is impure both outwardly and inwardly, so it is not lawful for them to enter al-Masjid al-Haram, which is Makkah and the sanctuary around it. From that day on, no polytheist entered Makkah. As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾ that is, destitution due to the cessation of the polytheists' attendance at the season, where they used to bring trade, buying and selling, which benefited the Muslims, ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, so prevent the polytheists and do not fear poverty. As for His saying: ﴿if He wills; indeed Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, it is an exception stated by Him, the Exalted, so that the hearts of the believers remain attached to Him, the Glorified and Exalted, hopeful, fearful, not complacent or heedless. His being Knowing and Wise implies the meaning mentioned, for one who possesses knowledge and wisdom places nothing except in its proper place. Therefore, whoever wishes the mercy or bounty of Allah must strive to be worthy of it, through faith and general and particular obedience.

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- The prohibition of self-admiration and admiration of one's deeds, for it, that is, admiration, is among the great obstacles to success.

2- Demonstration of Allah's bounty and generosity toward His believing servants.

3- Demonstration of the wisdom behind fighting in the way of Allah, the Exalted.

4- Affirmation of the disbeliever's inner (spiritual) impurity.

5- Prohibition of a polytheist entering the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah, whoever he may be, unlike the other mosques, where a disbeliever may be permitted to enter with the permission of the Muslims for a benefit.

6- Fear of poverty and need should not prevent the believer from complying with the command of his Lord, for Allah, the Exalted, has guaranteed enrichment, if He wills.

Idh a'jabatkum kathratukum (إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم): that is, the abundance of your numbers, to the point that some said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers."

Fa lam tughni 'ankum shay'an (فلم تغن عنكم شيئاً): that is, it did not avail you anything of any benefit when you were routed at the outset of the encounter.

Wa daqat 'alaykumu al-ard (وضاقت عليكم الأرض): that is, you did not know where to go or how to act, as if you were confined to a narrow place.

Bima rahubat (بما رحبت): that is, despite its breadth and vastness.

Anzala Allahu sakinatahu (أنزل الله سكينته): that is, tranquility in their souls, so that anxiety and agitation departed.

Wa anzala junudan (وأنزل جنوداً): that is, of the angels.

Najas (نجس): that is, possessors of impurity, due to the corruption of their souls through shirk.

Ba'da 'amihim hadha (بعد عامهم هذا): the year nine after the Hijra.

'Aylah (عيلة): that is, poverty, destitution, and need.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah forbade the believers to take disbelievers as allies, even if they were their relatives, and warned them against holding back from emigration and jihad—and since what usually kept a person from this was cowardice and fear—He informed them in these three verses that He is their helper and supporter, so that cowardice and fear should not keep them from fulfilling the duty of emigration and jihad. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has given you victory in many battlefields﴾ such as Badr, al-Nadir, Qurayzah, the Conquest, and others, ﴿and on the day of Hunayn﴾ when they fought the tribe of Hawazin, reminding them of a defeat that befell the believers as a result of an error by some of them, namely being deluded by the abundance of their numbers, when some of them said: "We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers." They were twelve thousand, while their enemy was only four thousand. As soon as they penetrated between the sides of the valley, the enemy rained upon them a torrent of arrows and javelins, and they did not know how to act, until the earth became narrow for them despite its breadth, and they turned back fleeing in retreat. None remained firm except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was on his white mule called "al-Duldul," with al-'Abbas at his side and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, his cousin. Then the caller of the Messenger of Allah called out: "O companions of Surat al-Baqarah, come! O companions of the tree (the tree of the Pledge of al-Ridwan), come!" So they returned to the battle, and its wheel turned. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts﴾ which touched the hearts and breathed into them the spirit of courage, patience, and steadfastness. So they persevered and fought, and within an hour the enemy was taken captive before them. Never had they gained booty like what they gained that day, for the number of camels reached twelve thousand camels, and of sheep there was an uncountable and unnumbered amount. Thus came His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your great numbers pleased you but they availed you nothing, and the earth was confined for you despite its vastness, then you turned back fleeing﴾ that is, fleeing from the enemy. ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts﴾ that is, of angels ﴿which you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved﴾ that is, Hawazin. ﴿And that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, that is, the killing and captivity.

As for His saying: ﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills﴾ that is, after your fighting against the disbelievers and your killing of those you killed, Allah relents to whomever He wills of those who remained alive after the battle. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ He forgives those among the polytheists whom He accepts in repentance their past sins of shirk and all other sins, and shows them mercy by admitting them to Paradise along with whomever He wills of the believers who are sincere in their faith. This is what the three verses indicate. As for the fourth verse: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are impure, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾ He, the Exalted, commanded the believers to prevent every polytheist man and woman from entering al-Masjid al-Haram, because the polytheist is impure both outwardly and inwardly, so it is not lawful for them to enter al-Masjid al-Haram, which is Makkah and the sanctuary around it. From that day on, no polytheist entered Makkah. As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾ that is, destitution due to the cessation of the polytheists' attendance at the season, where they used to bring trade, buying and selling, which benefited the Muslims, ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, so prevent the polytheists and do not fear poverty. As for His saying: ﴿if He wills; indeed Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, it is an exception stated by Him, the Exalted, so that the hearts of the believers remain attached to Him, the Glorified and Exalted, hopeful, fearful, not complacent or heedless. His being Knowing and Wise implies the meaning mentioned, for one who possesses knowledge and wisdom places nothing except in its proper place. Therefore, whoever wishes the mercy or bounty of Allah must strive to be worthy of it, through faith and general and particular obedience.

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- The prohibition of self-admiration and admiration of one's deeds, for it, that is, admiration, is among the great obstacles to success.

2- Demonstration of Allah's bounty and generosity toward His believing servants.

3- Demonstration of the wisdom behind fighting in the way of Allah, the Exalted.

4- Affirmation of the disbeliever's inner (spiritual) impurity.

5- Prohibition of a polytheist entering the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah, whoever he may be, unlike the other mosques, where a disbeliever may be permitted to enter with the permission of the Muslims for a benefit.

6- Fear of poverty and need should not prevent the believer from complying with the command of his Lord, for Allah, the Exalted, has guaranteed enrichment, if He wills.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 29:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day﴾: that is, not a sound belief that Allah the Exalted is pleased with, one that conforms to the truth and to reality.

﴿Nor do they forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾: that is, such as wine, usury (riba) and all the other prohibited things.

﴿Nor do they follow the religion of truth﴾: that is, Islam, since it is the religion that does not accept any religion other than itself.

﴿From among those who were given the Scripture﴾: that is, the Jews and the Christians.

﴿The jizyah﴾: that is, the known tax which the dhimmi (protected non-Muslim subject) pays every year.

﴿Willingly, while they are humbled﴾: that is, they hand it over with their own hands, not appointing anyone else to do so for them; and ﴿while they are humbled﴾: that is, abased and submissive to the rule of this Islam.

The meaning of the noble verse:

When Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger and the believers to fight the polytheists until they repent from polytheism, affirm the Oneness of God, and worship Allah the Exalted in accordance with what He has legislated, He then commanded His Messenger, in this verse, and the believers to fight the People of the Book, namely the Jews and the Christians, until they either submit to Islam or give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled. He made the giving of the jizyah the limit at which fighting ends, not Islam itself, because Islam is first presented to the People of the Book; if they accept it, that is well, and if they reject it, they are asked to enter the protection (dhimma) of the Muslims and their safeguarding under the emblem of the jizyah, which is a sign indicating their acceptance of the protection of the Muslims and their being governed by the law of Allah the Exalted. Once they give it, their blood is preserved, their property is safeguarded, and they are secure in their material and spiritual lives. This is what the noble verse contains: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, nor forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor follow the religion of truth, from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.﴾ If it is said that the Jews and the Christians believe in Allah and in the Last Day, how then does the verse deny that of them? The answer is that the Jews, in their belief in Allah, are anthropomorphists who liken Allah to His creation, attributing to Allah the Exalted attributes from which Allah is exalted far above; and the Christians believe that Allah incarnated in the Messiah, and that Allah is the third of three, whereas Allah is not like that. They therefore do not believe in Allah the Exalted as He is, the true God; so their belief is invalid and is not belief. In addition, if they had believed in Allah, they would have believed in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ); and if they had believed in the Last Day, they would have obeyed Allah and His Messenger in order to be saved from the punishment of the Last Day and to be made happy in it by entering Paradise. Since they did not believe and did not act, they were truly disbelievers, not believers. Allah the Mighty has spoken truly in denying them belief in Him and in the Last Day, and Allah knows best His creatures and what is within them.

Guidance from the noble verse:

From the guidance of the noble verse:

1- The obligation to fight the People of the Book until they submit or enter under the rule of Islam, in order to prepare them for Islam so that they may be perfected by it and made happy through it.

2- Belief that is not sound is not considered a belief that saves or brings happiness.

3- Considering lawful what Allah has forbidden of foods, drinks and marriages is manifest disbelief.

4- The legitimacy of taking the jizyah from the People of the Book; its amount is specified in the books of jurisprudence, and it varies according to a person's wealth or poverty, ease or hardship.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 30–33:

Explanation of the words:

ʿUzayr (ʿUzair): He is the one whom God caused to die for one hundred years and then raised up again. The Jews call him ʿIzrā.

al-Masīh (the Messiah): He is ʿĪsā son of Maryam, peace be upon them both.

Yuḍāhiʾūn: That is, they resemble.

Qawl alladhīna kafarū: That is, of their forefathers and ancestors who passed before them.

Qātalahum Allāh: That is, may God curse them because of their disbelief.

Anná yu'fakūn: That is, how are they turned away from the truth.

Aḥbārahum wa-ruhbānahum: al-Aḥbār is the plural of ḥibr, the scholars of the Jews; and al-Ruhbān is the plural of rāhib, the worshipper of the Christians.

Arbāban min dūn Allāh: That is, lords besides God, whom they take as legislators, so they act by their laws regarding what is lawful and unlawful.

Nūr Allāh: That is, Islam, because it is the guide to happiness and perfection in both abodes.

Bi-afwāhihim: That is, by lying against Him, slandering Him, and turning people away from Him.

Rasūlahu: Muhammad ﷺ.

The meaning of the verses:

When God, the Exalted, commanded fighting against the People of the Book because of their disbelief and their failure to have true faith that saves from the Fire, He mentioned in these three verses what establishes their disbelief and confirms it. He said, ﴿And the Jews say: ʿUzayr is the son of God﴾. Ascribing a son to God, the Exalted, is disbelief in His majesty and perfection. ﴿And the Christians say: the Messiah is the son of God﴾. Ascribing a son to Him is disbelief in Him, Mighty and Majestic, and in His majesty and perfection. As for the words of God, the Exalted, ﴿That is their saying with their mouths﴾, that means it has no basis in reality, since God has no son, and how could He have a son when He has no wife? It is merely their saying with their mouths. ﴿They imitate﴾, that is, they resemble, ﴿the saying of those who disbelieved before﴾, namely the earlier Jews and others. His words, ﴿God fight them; how are they deluded?﴾ are a supplication against them for curse and expulsion from God's mercy. His words, ﴿how are they deluded?﴾, mean how they are turned away from the truth and kept far from it in this strange manner. His words, ﴿They took their scholars and their monks as lords besides God﴾, are another proof of their disbelief and polytheism, since accepting the words of their scholars and worshippers, submitting to them and accepting them without question, to the point that they make lawful for them what is unlawful and forbid for them what is lawful, is polytheism and disbelief, God forbid. His words, ﴿and the Messiah son of Maryam﴾, mean that the Christians took him as a lord and a god. His words, ﴿Yet they were commanded only to worship one God﴾, mean that their prophets, such as Moses, Jesus, and others, commanded them only to worship God alone; there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him. His words, ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate﴾, declare God free of their polytheism. His words, ﴿They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, mean that the Jews and Christians wish to extinguish the light of God, which is Islam, with their mouths, through lies and fabrication, defamation and belittling. ﴿But God refuses except to perfect His light, though the disbelievers dislike it﴾. He has done so; to Him be praise and grace. Islam has become dominant over all religions. This is what the three verses indicate. As for the fourth verse [33], God, the Exalted, informs that ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger﴾, that is, Muhammad, ﴿with guidance﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿and the religion of truth﴾, which is Islam. His words, ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, mean that the true religion, which is Islam, will prevail over all religion, ﴿though the polytheists dislike it﴾.

He has done so, and Islam is manifest across the whole earth. The people of East and West have heard of it, and the people of East and West have embraced it. A day will come when Muslims will rule all the people of the world, by God's permission, the Exalted.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the disbelief of the Jews and Christians by mentioning their disbelieving beliefs.

2- Blind obedience to scholars and clergy, to the point that they make lawful and unlawful, and people follow them into polytheism.

3- Showing the enmity of the Jews and Christians toward Islam and their cooperation in corrupting it and corrupting its adherents.

4- Good news for Muslims that they will rule the world one day, and Islam will become the religion by which God is worshipped on earth, and no other. This is witnessed by the verse ﴿and religion will be entirely for God﴾ [al-Anfal: 39]. If God did not know that this would occur, He would not have made it an aim and urged us to reach it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 34–35:

Explanation of the words:

"Bil-batil" (falsely): i.e., without any right that would have permitted them to take it.

"Wa yasudduna 'an sabilillah" (and they turn away from the way of Allah): i.e., they turn themselves and others away from Islam, which is the path that leads the servant to the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted.

"Yaknizun" (hoard): they gather wealth and bury it, out of fear for it, and do not pay its due right.

"Al-dhahab wal-fiddah" (gold and silver): these are the well-known two currencies.

"Fi sabilillah" (in the way of Allah): i.e., in what pleases Allah, such as jihad and feeding the poor and the needy.

"Fabashshirhum" (so give them good tidings): i.e., inform them of a painful punishment, meaning a painful, aching one.

"Yuha 'alayha" (it will be heated upon it): because it is turned into plates, and it is heated, then their foreheads are branded with it.

"Hadha ma kanaztum" (this is what you hoarded): i.e., it will be said to them at the time of their being branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves," as a rebuke and reproach to them.

The meaning of the two verses:

In connection with the mention of the hostility of the Jews and Christians toward Islam and the Muslims, and that they constantly and always want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, the Exalted mentioned what is a clear indication that they are materialists who have no concern except wealth and leadership. So He informed the Muslims, saying: ﴿O you who believe, indeed many of the rabbis﴾, who are the scholars of the Jews, ﴿and the monks﴾, who are the men of the churches among the Christians, ﴿consume the wealth of people falsely﴾, such as bribery and the writing of indulgence certificates, which they sell to the lowly among them, along with other tricks carried out in the name of religion. His saying about them, ﴿and they turn away from the way of Allah﴾, is clear evidence that they continually fight Islam in order to preserve their religious positions, living off them and lording over the lowly and common people among the Jews and Christians. His saying ﴿and those who hoard gold and silver﴾ is a general expression that includes the rabbis, the monks, and others among all people, from the Muslims and from the People of the Book; however, the rabbis and monks are included by the expression first, because whoever consumes people's wealth falsely and turns away from the way of Allah is more likely to hoard gold and silver and not spend it in the way of Allah. His saying to His Messenger ﴿so give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ means: inform them, giving them the news in the form of good tidings in advance. He explained the kind of painful punishment with His saying ﴿on the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾, meaning the plates of gold and silver after being turned into plates, ﴿and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with them﴾, meaning from all four directions: from the front, from behind, from the right, and from the left. It will be said to them in mockery and contempt, and this is a kind of punishment more severe on the soul than physical punishment: ﴿This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.﴾

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Clarification of the reality of the scholars of the Jews and Christians: they are materialists who have sold their hereafter for their worldly life, fighting Islam and turning away from it in order to preserve leadership and to eat at the expense of Islam.

2- The prohibition of consuming people's wealth falsely.

3- The prohibition of gathering wealth, hoarding it, and not spending from it.

4- Wealth whose zakat is paid every year is not called a hoard, even if it is buried under the earth.

5- Clarification of the punishment of one who hoards wealth and does not spend from it in the way of Allah, and it is a severe punishment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 36–37:

Explanation of the words:

ʿIddah (ʿiddah): meaning "number."

Ash-shuhur (ash-shuhūr): the plural of shahr (month); a month is twenty-nine days or thirty days.

Fi kitab Allah (fī kitāb Allāh): meaning the Book of Decrees, the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Arba'atun hurum (arba'atun ḥurum): these are Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram. Each one of them is ḥarām (sacred), and the plural is ḥurum.

Ad-din al-qayyim (ad-dīn al-qayyim): meaning the upright law that contains no crookedness.

Fa-la tazlimu fihinna anfusakum (fa-lā taẓlimū fīhinna anfusakum): meaning, do not commit sins in the sacred months, for they are more gravely sacred.

Kaffah (kāffah): meaning all together, and in all the months, both their lawful and their sacred.

Ma'a al-muttaqin (maʿa al-muttaqīn): meaning with support and victory; and the muttaqun (the God-fearing) are those who do not disobey Allah, exalted is He.

Innama an-nasi' (innamā an-nasīʾ): meaning the postponement of the sanctity of the month of Muharram to Safar.

Yuhilluna hu ʿaman wa yuharrimunahu ʿaman (yuḥillūnahu ʿāman wa yuḥarrimūnahu ʿāman): meaning, they make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year.

Liyuwati'u ʿiddata ma harrama Allah (li-yuwāṭiʾū ʿiddata mā ḥarrama Allāh): meaning, so that they match the number of the sacred months, which are four.

Zuyyina lahum su'u a'malihim (zuyyina lahum sūʾu aʿmālihim): meaning, Satan made this postponement of the sacred month seem attractive to them, and it is an evil deed, because it is an encroachment upon the Lawgiver and a trick to make the forbidden lawful.

Meaning of the two verses

The context returned to speak of the polytheists after that digression about the People of the Book. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾, which are not to be increased or decreased, and that it is so in the Preserved Tablet, ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾. Among them are four sacred months, meaning forbidden ones, and they are Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram. Allah made them sacred, meaning He made fighting in them forbidden, so that they would be a truce during which the Arabs could travel for trade and for the Hajj and ʿUmrah without fearing anyone. When Islam came and Allah honored its people, the sanctity of fighting in them was abrogated (naskh). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿That is the upright religion﴾ means that the prohibition of these months and their honoring by not fighting in them is the upright law. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ means do not commit sins and acts of disobedience in the sacred months, for that necessitates the anger and wrath of Allah upon you, so do not expose yourselves to it. His saying, ﴿And fight the polytheists﴾ is an address to the believers, commanding them, exalted is He, to fight the polytheists after the period allotted to them has ended, which is four months. His saying ﴿all together﴾ means all of you, with none of you lagging behind, just as they fight you together, so unite among yourselves in fighting them. His saying ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾, who are those who guard themselves against polytheism and sins, means that Allah is with you through His help and support against the disobedient polytheists. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ means that postponing the sanctity of a sacred month to Safar, as the people of ignorance did, in order to make fighting in the sacred month lawful through this satanic fatwa, this postponement is an increase in the disbelief of the disbelievers, because it is opposition to the law of Allah, and it is disbelief with certainty, based on His saying, exalted is He, ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾, meaning through the postponement they increase in misguidance beyond their misguidance. His saying ﴿They make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year﴾ refers to the postponement, which is the month they postponed, meaning they postponed its sanctity to the month after it so that they could fight in the sacred month. So they make it lawful one year and sacred another year, until they match the number of the sacred months, without increase or decrease, thinking that they were not disobeying while concealed by this satanic fatwa, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾, and the one who makes falsehood attractive with certainty is Satan.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ informs that He, Mighty and Majestic, does not guide the disbelieving people to what is true and good, and that is a punishment for them for their disbelief in Him and His Messenger, and their persistence in that.

Guidance from the two verses

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Clarification that the months of the Hijri year are twelve months, and its days are three hundred and fifty-four days.

2- Clarification that the sacred months are four, and the Messenger (ﷺ) explained them: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram.

3- The sanctity of the sacred months, and the multiplication of evil deeds in them, meaning the gravity of sins committed in them.

4- The attribute of Allah's companionship, which is a special companionship of help and support for those who are God-fearing.

5- The prohibition of tricking the Law through false fatwas to make the forbidden lawful, and that such trickery is nothing but an increase in sin.

6- Making falsehood attractive and beautifying wrongdoing is from Satan.

7- The deprivation of the people of disbelief and wickedness from Allah's guidance and success toward what is true and good, in state and in outcome.

Liyuwati'u ʿiddata ma harrama Allah (li-yuwāṭiʾū ʿiddata mā ḥarrama Allāh): meaning, so that they match the number of the sacred months, which are four.

Zuyyina lahum su'u a'malihim (zuyyina lahum sūʾu aʿmālihim): meaning, Satan made this postponement of the sacred month seem attractive to them, and it is an evil deed, because it is an encroachment upon the Lawgiver and a trick to make the forbidden lawful.

Meaning of the two verses

The context returned to speak of the polytheists after that digression about the People of the Book. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾, which are not to be increased or decreased, and that it is so in the Preserved Tablet, ﴿the day He created the heavens and the earth﴾. Among them are four sacred months, meaning forbidden ones, and they are Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram. Allah made them sacred, meaning He made fighting in them forbidden, so that they would be a truce during which the Arabs could travel for trade and for the Hajj and ʿUmrah without fearing anyone. When Islam came and Allah honored its people, the sanctity of fighting in them was abrogated (naskh). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿That is the upright religion﴾ means that the prohibition of these months and their honoring by not fighting in them is the upright law. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ means do not commit sins and acts of disobedience in the sacred months, for that necessitates the anger and wrath of Allah upon you, so do not expose yourselves to it. His saying, ﴿And fight the polytheists﴾ is an address to the believers, commanding them, exalted is He, to fight the polytheists after the period allotted to them has ended, which is four months. His saying ﴿all together﴾ means all of you, with none of you lagging behind, just as they fight you together, so unite among yourselves in fighting them. His saying ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾, who are those who guard themselves against polytheism and sins, means that Allah is with you through His help and support against the disobedient polytheists. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ means that postponing the sanctity of a sacred month to Safar, as the people of ignorance did, in order to make fighting in the sacred month lawful through this satanic fatwa, this postponement is an increase in the disbelief of the disbelievers, because it is opposition to the law of Allah, and it is disbelief with certainty, based on His saying, exalted is He, ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾, meaning through the postponement they increase in misguidance beyond their misguidance. His saying ﴿They make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year﴾ refers to the postponement, which is the month they postponed, meaning they postponed its sanctity to the month after it so that they could fight in the sacred month. So they make it lawful one year and sacred another year, until they match the number of the sacred months, without increase or decrease, thinking that they were not disobeying while concealed by this satanic fatwa, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾, and the one who makes falsehood attractive with certainty is Satan.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ informs that He, Mighty and Majestic, does not guide the disbelieving people to what is true and good, and that is a punishment for them for their disbelief in Him and His Messenger, and their persistence in that.

Guidance from the two verses

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Clarification that the months of the Hijri year are twelve months, and its days are three hundred and fifty-four days.

2- Clarification that the sacred months are four, and the Messenger (ﷺ) explained them: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram.

3- The sanctity of the sacred months, and the multiplication of evil deeds in them, meaning the gravity of sins committed in them.

4- The attribute of Allah's companionship, which is a special companionship of help and support for those who are God-fearing.

5- The prohibition of tricking the Law through false fatwas to make the forbidden lawful, and that such trickery is nothing but an increase in sin.

6- Making falsehood attractive and beautifying wrongdoing is from Satan.

7- The deprivation of the people of disbelief and wickedness from Allah's guidance and success toward what is true and good, in state and in outcome.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 38–40:

Explanation of the words:

Ma lakum? (What is the matter with you?): i.e., what excuses have become established for you?

Infiru (go forth): i.e., go out hastily and eagerly.

Ithaqaltum (you were weighed down): i.e., you were slow, as if you were carrying heavy burdens.

Illa tansuruhu (if you do not support him): i.e., the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

Thani ithnayn (the second of two): i.e., he and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him).

Fi al-ghar (in the cave): the cave of Thawr, i.e., in a mountain in Makkah called Thawr.

Li-sahibihi (to his companion): this is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him).

Sakinatahu (his tranquility): i.e., his peace of mind.

Kalimat alladhina kafaru (the word of those who disbelieved): this is the call to polytheism.

Al-suflaa (the lowest): i.e., defeated, brought low, with no voice heard for it.

Wa kalimatu Allah hiya al-ulya (and the word of Allah is the highest): i.e., the call to monotheism ("There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah") is the highest, the dominant and the evident one.

Meaning of the verses:

These verses were revealed concerning the Battle of Tabuk. The Prophet (ﷺ) received word that Heraclius, king of the Romans, had gathered his armies to fight the Messenger (ﷺ), so the Prophet (ﷺ) declared a general mobilization. The time was a hot summer, the land was in drought and famine, and this was in Shawwal of the year nine. This expedition was named the Expedition of Hardship (Ghazwat al-'Usrah). So the Lord, blessed and exalted, urged the believers to go out with their Prophet to fight his enemies who had resolved to attack him in his own homeland. Thus He, exalted, revealed His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you incline heavily toward the earth?﴾ The one who said it was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Go forth in the cause of Allah﴾, i.e., go out to jihad ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾, i.e., for the sake of His pleasure, glorified and exalted is He, and for what is with Him of lasting bliss. As for His saying ﴿What is [wrong] with you?﴾, i.e., what is it that prevents you from going forth? While you are believers, seekers of perfection and felicity in both abodes. As for His saying ﴿you incline heavily toward the earth﴾, i.e., you were slow to set out, content to remain in your homes and lands. ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter?﴾ Allah, exalted, rebukes those who were in this state among them, then says to them: ﴿Then the enjoyment of worldly life is but little compared to the Hereafter﴾, i.e., all that exists in it of enjoyments of various kinds, compared with the lasting bliss in the Hereafter in the neighborhood of the Lord of the worlds, ﴿is but little﴾, trivial and of no worth. How, then, do you prefer the little over the much, and the perishable over the everlasting? Then He said to them: ﴿If you do not go forth﴾, i.e., if you abandon supporting him (ﷺ) and leave him to go out to fight the Romans alone, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent﴾. In this report there is a severe warning that moved the hearts of the believers.

As for His saying, exalted: ﴿If you do not support him﴾, i.e., if you forsake him and do not go out with him in this difficult situation, then Allah has already supported him in a situation more difficult than this, at the time when those who disbelieved drove him out: ﴿the second of two﴾, i.e., he and Abu Bakr alone, ﴿when they were in the cave﴾, i.e., the cave of Thawr, ﴿when he said to his companion﴾, when he said, "If one of them looked beneath his feet, he would see us, O Messenger of Allah": ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.﴾ ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him﴾, so his soul was calmed, he was at peace, and fear departed from his heart. ﴿And He supported him with soldiers you did not see﴾, ﴿and made the word of those who disbelieved﴾, which is their call to polytheism, ﴿the lowest﴾, defeated and brought low, ﴿while the word of Allah﴾, the word "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," ﴿is the highest﴾, the dominant and evident one. ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might﴾, the Mighty who is not overcome, ﴿Wise﴾ in His disposal and management, granting victory to whom He wills without hindrance and defeating whom He wills without any opponent.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The obligation to go out to jihad when the leader calls for a general summons, which is known as general mobilization or the general call to arms (al-nafir al-'amm).

2. The mobilization must be in the cause of Allah, not in a cause other than His way, exalted is He.

3. Clarification of the worthlessness and insignificance of the worldly life compared with the Hereafter.

4. The obligation to support the Messenger (ﷺ) in his religion, his community, and his sunnah.

5. The nobility of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and the explanation of his virtue.

6. Islam is exalted and nothing is exalted above it.
