Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 41–43:

Explanation of the words:

Khifafan wa thiqalan (light and heavy): al-khifaf is the plural of khafif, meaning a young man strong in body and possessing provision and mount. Al-thiqal is the plural of thaqil, meaning an old man, a sick person, or a poor person who has no provision.

Dhalikum (that): that is, striving in jihad with wealth and self is better for you than inclining to the earth and abandoning jihad, both in the present and in the outcome.

ʿArḍan qarīban (a near gain): spoils in a nearby place, not far away.

Aw safaran qāṣidan (or a moderate journey): that is, moderate, without hardship in it.

Al-shuqqa (the distance): the long road that cannot be covered except with hardship and toil.

ʿAfā Allāh ʿanka (may God pardon you): He did not take you to account.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the urging to go out to fight the Romans in al-Sham. In these verses, Exalted is He commands the believers to go out to jihad in every condition, whether in strength or weakness. Let the young strong man go out, as well as the elderly weak one, and the wealthy as well as the poor. So He, Exalted, said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your selves﴾ against the enemies of God who disbelieve in Him and His Messenger, until they enter Islam or give the jizya and accept the rulings of Islam. ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾: that is, your going forth for jihad and your fighting of the disbelievers until you reach one of the two good ends is better for you than settling into the earth and being content with the life of this world, which is a little enjoyment, if you knew that.

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed long to them﴾. Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: Had those who stayed behind from jihad, from the hypocrites and those weak in faith, been called to a near gain, that is, present spoils, or to an easy, moderate journey, they would have followed you and gone out with you. But you called them to Tabuk, in the time of heat and need, so the distance became long for them, and they made excuses to you and stayed behind.

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they will swear by God﴾, that is, to you, saying: ﴿If we had been able﴾, that is, to go out, ﴿we would have gone out with you.﴾ Exalted said: ﴿They destroy themselves﴾, in that they bring upon themselves the wrath of God and His punishment, ﴿and God knows that they are liars﴾ in everything for which they offered excuses. This is what the first and second verses [41–42] indicate. As for the third verse, it contains the reproach of God, Exalted, to His Prophet ﷺ, in that he granted permission to those who asked him to stay behind from going forth and rising up to Tabuk. It was part of sound policy not to grant permission to anyone until the truthful is distinguished from the liar by it. Exalted said: ﴿God pardon you﴾, that is, He overlooked you and did not take you to account. He placed this expression before the reproach contained in the interrogation ﴿Why did you give them permission?﴾ to hasten joy to the Prophet ﷺ, for had it been delayed beyond the whole reproach, it would have produced fear and sorrow. And His saying, Exalted: ﴿until those who were truthful became clear to you and you knew the liars﴾ is the reason for the reproach over granting permission to the hypocrites to stay behind from going forth to Tabuk.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- When the imam declares general mobilization, it is forbidden to stay behind from jihad, and no one may sit out except with permission, for a reason that applies to him, so he asks permission and it is granted.

2- Jihad is by self and also by wealth, and it is better than abandoning it, both in the present and in the outcome.

3- False oaths, whether to nullify a right or to establish falsehood, entail the wrath of God Exalted and His punishment.

4- The legitimacy of reproach toward the beloved.

5- The permissibility of acting against what is better (al-awla) on the part of the Prophet ﷺ, due to his not knowing what God had not taught him.

5- The permissibility of acting against what is better (al-awla) on the part of the Prophet ﷺ, due to his not knowing what God had not taught him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 41–43:

Explanation of the words:

Khifafan wa thiqalan (light and heavy): al-khifaf is the plural of khafif, meaning a young man strong in body and possessing provision and mount. Al-thiqal is the plural of thaqil, meaning an old man, a sick person, or a poor person who has no provision.

Dhalikum (that): that is, striving in jihad with wealth and self is better for you than inclining to the earth and abandoning jihad, both in the present and in the outcome.

ʿArḍan qarīban (a near gain): spoils in a nearby place, not far away.

Aw safaran qāṣidan (or a moderate journey): that is, moderate, without hardship in it.

Al-shuqqa (the distance): the long road that cannot be covered except with hardship and toil.

ʿAfā Allāh ʿanka (may God pardon you): He did not take you to account.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the urging to go out to fight the Romans in al-Sham. In these verses, Exalted is He commands the believers to go out to jihad in every condition, whether in strength or weakness. Let the young strong man go out, as well as the elderly weak one, and the wealthy as well as the poor. So He, Exalted, said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your selves﴾ against the enemies of God who disbelieve in Him and His Messenger, until they enter Islam or give the jizya and accept the rulings of Islam. ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾: that is, your going forth for jihad and your fighting of the disbelievers until you reach one of the two good ends is better for you than settling into the earth and being content with the life of this world, which is a little enjoyment, if you knew that.

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed long to them﴾. Exalted says to His Messenger ﷺ: Had those who stayed behind from jihad, from the hypocrites and those weak in faith, been called to a near gain, that is, present spoils, or to an easy, moderate journey, they would have followed you and gone out with you. But you called them to Tabuk, in the time of heat and need, so the distance became long for them, and they made excuses to you and stayed behind.

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿And they will swear by God﴾, that is, to you, saying: ﴿If we had been able﴾, that is, to go out, ﴿we would have gone out with you.﴾ Exalted said: ﴿They destroy themselves﴾, in that they bring upon themselves the wrath of God and His punishment, ﴿and God knows that they are liars﴾ in everything for which they offered excuses. This is what the first and second verses [41–42] indicate. As for the third verse, it contains the reproach of God, Exalted, to His Prophet ﷺ, in that he granted permission to those who asked him to stay behind from going forth and rising up to Tabuk. It was part of sound policy not to grant permission to anyone until the truthful is distinguished from the liar by it. Exalted said: ﴿God pardon you﴾, that is, He overlooked you and did not take you to account. He placed this expression before the reproach contained in the interrogation ﴿Why did you give them permission?﴾ to hasten joy to the Prophet ﷺ, for had it been delayed beyond the whole reproach, it would have produced fear and sorrow. And His saying, Exalted: ﴿until those who were truthful became clear to you and you knew the liars﴾ is the reason for the reproach over granting permission to the hypocrites to stay behind from going forth to Tabuk.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- When the imam declares general mobilization, it is forbidden to stay behind from jihad, and no one may sit out except with permission, for a reason that applies to him, so he asks permission and it is granted.

2- Jihad is by self and also by wealth, and it is better than abandoning it, both in the present and in the outcome.

3- False oaths, whether to nullify a right or to establish falsehood, entail the wrath of God Exalted and His punishment.

4- The legitimacy of reproach toward the beloved.

5- The permissibility of acting against what is better (al-awla) on the part of the Prophet ﷺ, due to his not knowing what God had not taught him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 44–46:

Explanation of the words:

Lā yasta'dhinūnaka: that is, they do not ask you for permission to stay behind from jihad.

Wa-ertābat qulūbuhum: that is, their hearts doubted the truth of what you call to of the true religion.

Fī raybihim: that is, in their doubt.

Yataraddadūn: bewildered, unable to remain firm on anything.

La-a'addū lahu 'uddah: they would have prepared for it what is necessary of weapons, provisions and mounts.

Inbi'āthahum: that is, their going out with you.

Fa-thabbaṭahum: He cast into their souls the desire to stay behind and made it beloved to them, so they became lazy and did not go out.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of the Battle of Tabuk and the condition of those ordered to march forth in it. After Allah the Exalted rebuked His Messenger for granting permission to those who stayed behind, He informed him that the sincere believers do not ask him for permission to stay behind from jihad with their wealth and their selves. Rather, the ones who ask him are ﴿those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt﴾ concerning the faith in Allah, His Messenger, His promise and His threat. They are bewildered and wavering, not knowing where to turn, and this is the state of one whose creed is unsteady, like all the hypocrites. He, the Exalted, also informed him that they are liars in their excuses, for had they wished to go out, they would have prepared for it its equipment, that is, they would have readied its necessities of weapons, provisions and a riding animal. But they were resolved not to go out under any circumstances, and had you not granted them permission to stay behind, they would have stayed behind, opposing your intention and defying your command. This is because Allah the Exalted disliked their going out, for it contained harm and danger, so He held them back by what He cast into their hearts of weakness and into their bodies of laziness, as if it were said to them: "Sit with those who sit." This is what the verse [44] indicates: ﴿Had they wished to go out, they would certainly have prepared for it some equipment, but Allah disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said: "Remain behind with those who remain behind."﴾ And His saying, the Exalted, at the end of the first verse [44]: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-conscious﴾ affirms His knowledge of the conditions and souls of His servants, so what He informs of is the truth and the reality. The sincere believers do not seek to stay behind from jihad because of their faith and God-consciousness, while the hypocrites are those who seek to stay behind because of their doubt and wickedness, and Allah knows best about them, and none informs you like the One who is All-Aware.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The excellence of faith and God-consciousness, for whoever possesses them cannot stay behind from jihad with self and wealth.

2- The danger of doubt in creed, and that it is the cause of bewilderment and hesitation, and its possessor is unable to strive with wealth or self.

3- Prior evil tendencies come between their owner and doing good.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 47–48:

Explanation of the words:

"Had they gone out among you": i.e., slipping in among your men.

"Except to increase you in corruption": corruption in opinion and planning.

"They would have hastened between your ranks": i.e., they would have rushed among you with tale-bearing (namimah), incitement and stirring up strife, to keep you in turmoil.

"And among you are listeners to them": i.e., among you are those who listen to them a great deal and are affected by their inciting and corrupt words.

"Before": i.e., when you came to Madinah as an emigrant.

"And they plotted against you": through deceit, scheming, contacting the Jews and polytheists, and cooperating with them.

"And the command of Allah prevailed": by the conquest of Makkah and people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes.

"While they were averse": i.e., to the coming of the truth and the prevalence of Allah's command through the victory of His religion.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in exposing the intentions of the hypocrites and lifting the veil from them. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Had they gone out among you﴾, O Messenger and believers, i.e., to the expedition of Tabuk, ﴿they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾, i.e., harm, corruption and confusion of the believers' thoughts through the poisonous speech they would spread for discouragement and demoralization. ﴿And they would have hastened through your ranks﴾, i.e., rushed their mounts ﴿between you﴾, i.e., among your ranks, with words of discouragement and dispiritment, ﴿seeking to cause you fitnah﴾ by that, and fitnah is the dispersal of your assembly and the stirring up of enmity among you, by means of the wicked and corrupt speech that the hypocrites excel at in every time and place. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among you are listeners to them﴾, i.e., among you, O believers, are weak in faith who listen to you and convey to them the news of your secrets, just as among you are those who listen to them and obey them. For this reason, and for others, Allah disliked their setting out and held them back, so they sat with those who sat behind: the women, the children, the infirm and the sick. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, who work to nullify His religion and defeat His allies. Therefore He turned them away from going out with you to fight your enemies, the Romans and the Arabs who had become Christian in Syria.

His saying, Exalted is He, in the second verse [48]: ﴿They had certainly sought fitnah before﴾, indeed from the day you emigrated to Madinah and found Islam established there, they were stirring up strife among your companions in order to bring about their downfall. At Uhud, Ibn Ubayy withdrew with a third of the army, namely Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, intending to turn back from the fighting had Allah not protected them. ﴿And they plotted against you the affairs﴾, turning them in various directions with the aim of eliminating your call, so they backed the polytheists and the Jews on many occasions, and this was their habit. ﴿Until the truth came﴾ by the conquest of Makkah, ﴿and the command of Allah prevailed﴾ by the entry of most of the Arabs into the religion of Allah, ﴿while they were averse﴾ to that; rather, they were grieved and saddened. Therefore, do not grieve over their not going out with you, and do not concern yourselves with it or be bothered by it, for Allah, out of mercy toward you and support for you, turned them away from going out with you. So praise Allah and extol Him as He deserves, and to Allah belong praise and favour.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The presence of hypocrites among the ranks of the believers is a danger to them and a great harm to them; therefore they should not be included in any matter, nor should they be relied upon for any mission.

2- The obligation to take precaution in matters of importance and consequence for the life of Islam and the Muslims.

3- The hypocrite is distressed by the honour of Islam and the Muslims and grieves over it.

4- Allah's management of His allies is the best management; therefore it is obligatory to be content with Allah's decree and destiny and to submit to it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 49–52:

Explanation of the words:

Among them: that is, among the hypocrites, and he is al-Jadd ibn Qays.

Permit me: that is, to stay behind from the jihad.

And do not tempt me: that is, do not put me into temptation (fitnah), on the claim that if he sees the women of the Romans he will not be able to control himself.

A good fortune that distresses them: "good fortune" (hasanah) is everything good, such as victory, booty, and well-being; "distresses them" means they are grieved by it and saddened.

We had already taken our precaution: that is, we took precautions regarding the matter, which is why we did not go out with them.

One of the two good outcomes: the first is victory over the enemy and triumph over them, and the second is martyrdom, which brings inheritance of Paradise.

So wait: that is, wait, for we are with you among those who wait.

The meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me permission and do not put me to temptation."﴾ That is, permission to stay behind from jihad, ﴿and do not put me to temptation﴾ by compelling me to go out; that is, do not put me into temptation. It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Would you like to go to the lands of Banu al-Asfar?" He said: "I am infatuated with women, and I fear that if I see the women of Banu al-Asfar (who are the Romans), I will not be able to restrain myself and will be tempted." The one who said this was al-Jadd ibn Qays, one of the leaders of the hypocrites in Madinah. So God, exalted is He, said, as a curse upon him and a refutation of his falsehood: ﴿Surely into temptation they have fallen﴾. And what temptation is greater than shirk and hypocrisy? ﴿And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ — him and those like him from among the people of disbelief and hypocrisy. This is what the first verse indicates.

As for the second verse [50], it contains the disclosure of what the hypocrites say among themselves: that if a good fortune—victory or booty, and every good state—befalls the Messenger and the believers, it distresses them, that is, grieves and saddens them; and if a misfortune—defeat, killing, or death—befalls them, they say among themselves: ﴿We had already taken our precaution,﴾ that is, we took precaution regarding the matter, so we did not go out with them, ﴿and they turn away, returning to their homes and families, ﴿rejoicing﴾. This is what is contained in the verse, which is His saying: ﴿If good fortune befalls you, it distresses them; and if a misfortune befalls you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution," and they turn away, rejoicing.﴾

As for the third and fourth verses [51–52], God, exalted is He, taught His Messenger what to say, to enrage those hypocrites and to inform them of what would grieve them. So He said: ﴿Say: "Nothing will ever befall us except what God has decreed for us; He is our Protector, and upon God let the believers rely."﴾ That is, whether good or bad, nothing will befall us except what God has written for us, and what our Lord writes for us will only be good, because He is our Master. ﴿And upon God let the believers put their trust﴾—and we are believers, and upon our Lord we rely. He also told him: ﴿Say: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ That is, do you wait for us anything except one of the two good outcomes: victory and dominance over the people of shirk, disbelief and hypocrisy, or martyrdom in the way of God, followed by everlasting bliss in the neighborhood of the Lord of the worlds. And in response: ﴿So wait; indeed we are waiting with you.﴾ And we will not witness except what pleases us and grieves you.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The disgrace of al-Jadd ibn Qays, the recording of the curse upon him, and the announcement to him of Hell.

2- The clarification that the hypocrites and disbelievers rejoice at what grieves the Muslims, and are distressed at what pleases the Muslims, which is the prominent sign of hypocrisy in every hypocrite.

3- The obligation of relying upon God and not being concerned with the words of the hypocrites.

4- The clarification that the believers, in their jihad, face one of two choices: victory or martyrdom.

5- The legitimacy of speech that enrages the enemy and grieves him.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafsir) on Surah 9, verses 53–55:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Taw'an aw karhan* (willingly or unwillingly): meaning, whether you are willing or you are compelled to spend.

*Innakum kuntum qawman fasiqin* (indeed you have been a defiant people): this sentence gives the reason why their expenditures are not accepted. (*Fisq* here means defiant transgression against Allah's command.)

*Kusala* (lazy): reluctant, because they do not inwardly believe in the benefit of the prayer (*salah*).

*Fala tu'jibukum amwaluhum* (so do not let their wealth impress you): meaning, do not, O Muslims, find pleasing the wealth and children that the hypocrites (*munafiqun*) possess.

*Wa tazhaqa anfusuhum* (and their souls depart): meaning, they pass away and leave their bodies.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The context continues with Allah Most High teaching His Messenger (ﷺ) how to respond to the hypocrites. He said to him: Say to them, O Messenger, ﴿Spend, whether willingly or unwillingly﴾ and ﴿it will never be accepted from you﴾. That is, inform them that whatever they spend on this expedition to Tabuk and on other occasions, whether they spend it by choice or are compelled to do so, Allah will never accept it from them, because they have been a people of defiance, by their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger and their departure from obedience to both of them. This is what the first verse [53] indicates.

As for the second verse [54], Allah Most High informs us of the main reasons that prevented their expenditures from being accepted. These are: first, disbelief in Allah and His Messenger; second, that they come to the prayer only while lazy and reluctant; and third, their intense aversion to what they spend. Allah Most High says: ﴿Nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to prayer except while lazy, and they do not spend except while unwilling.﴾ This is what the second verse contains.

As for the third verse [55], Allah Most High forbids His Messenger and the believers from being impressed by their wealth and children, however great their abundance and beauty. So He says: ﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you.﴾ That is, do not find them pleasing, and do not tell them so. Allah Most High then explained to His Messenger the reason for giving them these things and increasing them, saying: ﴿Allah only intends to punish them through them in the worldly life and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers.﴾ The way in which they are punished by these things in this worldly life is that, when they spend wealth on zakah (obligatory almsgiving) and jihad (striving in the way of Allah), they feel a pain unlike any other, because they regard this spending as directed against them and not in their interest, since they do not wish the victory or dominance of Islam. As for their children, the punishment through them is that they see them entering Islam and acting by it, while they cannot turn them away from it. What greater inner pain could there be than a man's child rejecting his religion and adopting another? One of the conditions of that faith is to hate the disbeliever in it, even if he is one's father, mother, brother, sister, or closest relative. In addition to this, they die while disbelievers, passing from one punishment to a harsher one. By this, Allah the Lord consoles His Messenger and the believers, explaining the reason why He gave the hypocrites wealth and children: to punish them thereby, not to make them happy.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Establishing the principle that ostentation (*riya'*, showing off in worship) nullifies deeds, just as polytheism (*shirk*) nullifies them.
2. The application of the term *fisq* (defiance) to disbelief, so that every disbeliever is a defiant person in the absolute sense.
3. The prohibition of laziness in the prayer, and that this is a characteristic of the hypocrites (*munafiqun*).
4. The obligation to be content, within oneself, with what a servant spends in the way of Allah, whether as zakah or otherwise.
5. The dislike of a Muslim being impressed by the wealth and possessions of the people of defiance and hypocrisy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 56–59:

Explanation of the words:

Wa ma hum minkum (and they are not of you): that is, in inner reality, because they are disbelievers, and their faces and hearts are with the disbelievers.

Yafraqun (they are terrified): that is, they fear you with intense fear.

Multaja' (a refuge): that is, a fortified place to which they take refuge.

Aw magharat (or caves): plural of maghara, which is a cave in a mountain.

Aw mudkhalan (or a retreat): that is, a tunnel in the earth in which a frightened fugitive hides.

Yajmahun (they rush headlong): they hurry with a speed that cannot be resisted or halted.

Yalmizuka (they find fault with you): that is, they criticize you concerning the distribution of it and slander you.

Idha hum yaskhatun (they are displeased): that is, they are not content.

Hasbuna Allah (Allah is sufficient for us): that is, Allah suffices us in everything that concerns us.

Ila Allah raghibun (to Allah alone we turn in desire): that is, we hope and aspire to Allah alone.

The meanings of the verses:

The noble context continues to unmask the hypocrites, expose their faults and reveal their shameful conduct, so that whoever Allah has honoured with repentance may repent. Concerning them, the Exalted says: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you﴾, that is, of the people of your religion and faith. ﴿But they are not of you﴾, that is, in actual fact, since they are disbelievers and hypocrites. ﴿But they are a people who are terrified﴾, that is, they fear you intensely; therefore they swear to you that they are of you, so that you will grant them security for their lives and property. And to show the intensity of their terror of you and their fear of your swords, He says: ﴿If they could find a refuge﴾, that is, a fortress, ﴿or caves﴾, that is, hollows in the mountains, ﴿or a retreat﴾, that is, a tunnel in the earth, ﴿they would turn towards it﴾, that is, they would flee to it, ﴿rushing headlong﴾, that is, hastening so as to protect themselves from you. This is what the first and second verses indicate. As for the third and fourth verses [58–59], the Exalted informs that among the hypocrites are those who find fault with the Messenger ﷺ, that is, who slander him and criticize him concerning the distribution of the charities, accusing the Messenger ﷺ of not being just in the distribution. The Exalted says: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are content﴾, that is, with the Messenger and his distribution. ﴿But if they are not given from them, behold, they are displeased﴾. This is what the verse [58] contains. As for the final verse [59], Allah the Exalted guides them to what they ought to have been, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them﴾, that is, from the charities, ﴿and had said: "Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger, [He is the One who will provide]"﴾, that is, Allah suffices us, ﴿Allah will give us of His bounty﴾, the vast and great bounty, and His Messenger by what he distributes and apportions among us, ﴿indeed, to Allah we are turning in desire﴾ alone, ﴿hopeful and aspiring﴾, that is, it would have been better for them and more suitable to their needs.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1. False swearing is the emblem of the hypocrites. In a hadith: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

2. Cowardice, weakness, feebleness and fear are among the consequences of disbelief and hypocrisy.

3. Reviling the righteous and slandering them is a sign indicating the corruption of the hearts and intentions of the one who does so.

4. The manifestations of divine mercy appear in guiding the hypocrites to what is best for them, so that they may be perfected and be happy in both abodes.

5. There is no sufficiency except Allah, and it is obligatory that desire be confined to Him alone, without any other.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 56–59:

Explanation of the words:

Wa ma hum minkum (and they are not of you): that is, in inner reality, because they are disbelievers, and their faces and hearts are with the disbelievers.

Yafraqun (they are terrified): that is, they fear you with intense fear.

Multaja' (a refuge): that is, a fortified place to which they take refuge.

Aw magharat (or caves): plural of maghara, which is a cave in a mountain.

Aw mudkhalan (or a retreat): that is, a tunnel in the earth in which a frightened fugitive hides.

Yajmahun (they rush headlong): they hurry with a speed that cannot be resisted or halted.

Yalmizuka (they find fault with you): that is, they criticize you concerning the distribution of it and slander you.

Idha hum yaskhatun (they are displeased): that is, they are not content.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 60:

Explanation of the words:

Al-sadaqat (charities): the plural of sadaqah, which here means the obligatory zakat on wealth.

Lil-fuqara' (for the poor): the plural of faqir, who is one who does not have enough sustenance to meet his needs and does not beg from people.

Wal-masakin (and the needy): the plural of miskin, who is a poor person who does not have enough to meet his needs, who begs from people and humbles himself through begging.

Wal-'amilina 'alayha (and those employed to collect them): that is, to gather and collect them; they are the officials appointed for this task.

Wal-mu'allafati qulubuhum (and those whose hearts are to be reconciled): these are people whose acceptance of Islam is hoped for, or whose continued adherence to it is hoped for if they have already embraced it. They are people of standing and importance through whom Allah benefits if they become Muslims and their Islam is sound.

Wa-fi al-riqab (and for freeing slaves): that is, for the ransoming of necks, meaning their liberation from bondage, so that those seeking manumission (al-mukatabun) are given what they need to pay off the installments of their contract of manumission.

Wa-fi sabil Allah (and in the way of Allah): that is, jihad, for preparing equipment and providing the fighters with what they need in expenses.

Wa-ibn al-sabil (and the wayfarer): that is, the traveler cut off from his homeland, even if he is wealthy in his own land.

Fari-datan min Allah (as an obligation from Allah): that is, Allah, exalted is He, has made it an obligation upon His believing servants.

Meaning of the noble verse:

On the occasion of the hypocrites' slandering of the Messenger (ﷺ) and their criticism of his distribution of charities, Allah, exalted is He, in this noble verse specified the people who are particularly entitled to charities. By charities are meant the zakat and voluntary charity. He, mighty and majestic, said ﴿Indeed, the charities﴾, restricted to the eight categories mentioned, who are:

(1) The poor (al-fuqara'), who are the believers who do not find what meets their essential needs of food, drink, clothing and shelter.

(2) The needy (al-masakin), who are the poor who do not find what meets their needs and who do not abstain from begging; they ask people and display their neediness and want.

(3) Those employed to collect it, such as agents, collectors, clerks and distributors, who are given for their work the wage customary for such work in government service.

(4) Those whose hearts are to be reconciled (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum), who are those whose benefit to Islam and Muslims is hoped for, because of their positions and influence among their peoples. They are given from zakat to reconcile their hearts, that is, to gather them to Islam, to love it, to support it and to support its people. One of them may not yet have embraced Islam and is given to encourage him toward Islam, or he may be a Muslim whose Islam is weak and is given to strengthen and fortify him in Islam.

(5) For freeing slaves (fi al-riqab), which means helping those seeking manumission to pay their installments so that they may be freed. As for buying a slave with zakat and freeing him, it is not permitted, because the benefit returns to the giver of zakat, since the loyalty (wala') of the freed person belongs to him.

(6) The debtors (al-gharimin), plural of gharim, who are those upon whom debts have been incurred due to what they spent in obedience to Allah, exalted is He, on themselves and their dependents, and who have no wealth, neither cash nor goods, with which to pay their debts.

(7) For the way of Allah, which is equipping the fighters and spending on them for weapons, mounts, food and clothing.

(8) The wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), who are travelers who arrive in a land and their funds run out, so they are in need and are given from zakat, even if they are wealthy in their own lands.

As for His statement, exalted is He, ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾, meaning these charities and their distribution in this manner, Allah, exalted is He, has made it a binding obligation upon His believing servants. His statement ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ means of His creation and their circumstances, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His law and His distribution. Therefore it is never permitted to oppose this distribution, so that no one may be included to receive zakat who is not mentioned in this verse. It is not a condition that one give to all the categories; a person may give his zakat entirely to jihad, or to the poor and the needy, or to the debtors or the manumission-seekers, and that is valid, although it is better that he divide it among the mentioned categories that are present, since they may not all be found at the same time.

Guidance from the verse:

From the guidance of the verse:

1- Affirmation of the obligation of zakat.

2- Clarification of the disbursement of zakat.

3- The obligation of submission to Allah in His distribution, by not attempting to deviate from it.

4- Affirmation of the attributes of Allah, which here are: knowledge and wisdom. Whenever Allah is All-Knowing of His creation and their needs, and All-Wise in His disposal and His law, submission to His command and humble obedience and compliance become obligatory.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 61–63: Explanation of the words: *Yu'dhūna al-Nabiyya* (they harm the Prophet): that is, the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Harm (adha) is any disliked thing that befalls a person, whether much or little. *Huwa udhun* (he is an ear): that is, he listens to whoever speaks to him and talks with him, and this is a form of harm. *Qul udhunu khayrin lakum* (say: an ear of good for you): that is, he listens to whoever speaks to him without arrogance, but he acknowledges only the truth and accepts only what is good and right. So he is an ear of good for you, not an ear of evil like yourselves, O hypocrites. *Wa yu'minu lil-mu'minin* (and he believes the believers): that is, he trusts the sincere believers among the Emigrants and the Helpers. As for others, although he may listen to them, he does not believe them, because they are liars and wicked. *Wallahu ahaqqu an yur
đūhu wa rasūluhu ahaqqu an yurdūhu* (God has more right that they please Him, and His Messenger has more right that they please him): ... *Man yuhādidi Allaha wa rasūlahu* (whoever opposes God and His Messenger): that is, he opposes them and stands always in a limit (ḥadd) while they are in another limit, so there is no loyalty (walā') and no alliance (muwālāh), that is, no love and no support. Explanation of the verses: The noble context continues in exposing the hypocrites and clarifying their disgraceful conduct. God says: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet﴾, that is, among the hypocrites are individuals who harm the Prophet by slandering him and blaming him for things he is innocent of. God clarifies some of that harm, saying ﴿and they say, "He is an ear"﴾, that is, he listens to everything said to him. Far be it from him (ﷺ) to approve of listening to falsehood, evil or corruption; he listens only to what is good, even if it comes from a hypocrite who lies but speaks well. God commanded His Messenger to answer them with His words ﴿Say: "An ear of good for you"﴾, that is, he listens to what is good for you and does not listen to what is evil for you. Because he did not confront them with the badness of their deeds and the ugliness of their actions, this kindness and goodness led them to say ﴿He is an ear﴾, as a slander against him (ﷺ) and a defamation of him. God's words ﴿He believes in God and believes the believers﴾ are part of what the Messenger (ﷺ) was commanded to say to the hypocrites in reply to their falsehood: he (ﷺ) believes in God as Lord and God, and ﴿believes the believers﴾, that is, in their truthfulness regarding what they say. This is part of his goodness (ﷺ). His words ﴿and a mercy for those of you who believe﴾ are also part of his goodness: he (ﷺ) is a mercy for whoever believes in him and follows the light he brought, and through him they are perfected and made happy in their lives. God's words ﴿And those who harm the Messenger of God﴾, that is, by any kind of harm, small or great, God threatens them with His words ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾, which will certainly befall them, and they will surely taste it. This is what the first verse [61] indicates. As for the second verse [62], God informs us that the hypocrites swear to the believers that they did not slander the Messenger and did not say anything about him, intending by this to please the believers so that they would not strike them in retaliation for the honour of their Prophet. God says ﴿They swear to God to you, to please you; and God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾, that is, instead of pleasing the believers, they should have pleased God by repenting to Him and pleased the Messenger by faith and obedience, if they are truly believers as they claim. As for the third verse [63], God's words ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger﴾, that is, opposes and wars against them, then for him is the requital of his hostility and fighting: the fire of Hell, abiding in it forever. ﴿That is the great disgrace﴾, that is, being in the fire of Hell, abiding therein and never leaving it, is the great disgrace. Guidance from the verses: 1- The prohibition of harming the Messenger of God in any manner. 2- That the Prophet (ﷺ) is a mercy to the believers is a call to faith and Islam. 3- God's threat of painful punishment to whoever harms His Messenger is evidence of the disbelief of whoever harms the Messenger of God (ﷺ). 4- A demonstration of the lying and cowardice of the hypocrites, who swear to the believers that they did not slander the Messenger when they did slander him, and whose false oaths are meant to ward off the believers' anger and their retaliation. 5- The obligation to seek God's pleasure by doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes. 6- A threat of painful punishment against whoever opposes God and His Messenger.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Yahdharu al-munafiqun* (The hypocrites are wary): that is, they fear and guard themselves.

*Tunazzalu 'alayhim surah* (A surah would be sent down upon them): that is, concerning them, which would expose them by revealing their defect.

*Tunabbi'uhum bima fi qulubihim* (It would inform them of what is in their hearts): that is, it would tell them what they conceal within themselves.

*Qul istahzi'u* (Say: "Mock"): the command here is one of threat.

*Mukhrijun ma tahdharun* (Bringing forth what you fear): that is, its bringing forth from your souls, making it manifest to all people.

*Nakhudu wa nal'ab* (We were only conversing and playing): that is, we were conversing as is our custom and playing, we did not intend abuse or slander.

*Tastahzi'un* (You mock): that is, you ridicule and hold in contempt.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 67–70:

Explanation of the words:

Al-munafiqun (the hypocrites): those who show the believers faith with their tongues while concealing disbelief in their hearts.

Ba'duhum min ba'd (some of them are from others): i.e., they are alike in their belief, their speech and their deeds, so their affair is one.

Bil-munkar (what is forbidden): i.e., what the Sharia denies because of its harm or ugliness, which is disbelief in Allah and His Messenger.

'An al-ma'ruf (what is good): i.e., what the Sharia recognizes as beneficial and therefore commands, such as faith and righteous deeds.

Yaqbidun aydiyahum (they withhold their hands): i.e., they hold them back from spending in the way of Allah.

Nasu Allah fa-nasiyahum (they forgot Allah, so He forgot them): i.e., they abandoned Allah, so they did not believe in Him and His Messenger, and so He abandoned them and deprived them of His guidance and success.

'Adhab muqim (lasting punishment): i.e., enduring, which does not cease or perish.

Bi-khala-qihim (with their share): i.e., with their portion and lot of this world.

Wa-khadtum (and you immersed yourselves): i.e., in falsehood and vain talk.

Wal-mu'tafikat (the overturned cities): i.e., the places that were turned upside down, so their upper part became their lower part; they are three cities.

Bil-bayyinat (with clear proofs): the signs that indicate the truth of their messengers' mission to them.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to expose the hypocrites and clarify their characteristics, in the hope that they will repent. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another﴾, meaning they are like parts of a single thing, because their affair is one: they do not differ from one another in belief, speech or action. Allah then describes their state by saying: ﴿They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right﴾. This is evidence of their inversion and the corruption of their hearts and minds, since this is the opposite of what sensible people command. What is meant by the wrong they enjoin is disbelief and disobedience, and the right they forbid is faith in Allah and His Messenger and obedience to them. His words ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾ are a metaphor for holding back and not giving generously in spending in the way of Allah. His words ﴿They forgot Allah﴾ mean they did not believe in Him, did not believe in His Messenger, and did not obey Allah and His Messenger; ﴿so He forgot them﴾ means Allah left them deprived of all guidance, mercy and kindness. His words ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ confirm the meaning of ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾, for their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger is what deprived them of Allah's guidance, so they committed every kind of defiant disobedience and were the disobedient deserving of this description, namely defiance and immersion in it.

In verse [68], His words: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein; it is sufficient for them﴾, meaning it is enough for them as recompense, ﴿and Allah has cursed them, and they will have lasting punishment﴾, meaning enduring, which does not cease, perish or end. This verse contains the most severe warning for the people of hypocrisy and disbelief, for the Lord, the Exalted, threatens them with the fire of Hell, abiding therein, and with lasting punishment that will never leave them nor relent for a moment, forever and ever, after Allah has cursed them, distancing them and removing them from every mercy and good.

In the third verse [69], Allah commands His Messenger to say to the hypocrites who mock Allah, His signs and His Messenger: You, O hypocrites, are like those who were before you in being deluded by wealth and children, in disbelieving in Allah and denying His Messenger, until the punishment of Allah descended upon them and His custom of destroying them took its course. This is what the noble verse contains, when He says: ﴿Like those before you, who were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their share, and you have enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share﴾, meaning their portion that was decreed for them in this world, ﴿and you have immersed yourselves as they immersed﴾, meaning in falsehood, evil, disbelief and denial, ﴿like those who immersed﴾, meaning like their immersion, exactly alike, those who perished, ﴿their deeds became worthless in this world and the Hereafter﴾, meaning they vanished and were gone, and they gained nothing from them, ﴿and those are the losers﴾.

Since you, O hypocrites, follow their path in disbelief, denial and delusion by wealth and children, your fate will be like theirs, which is manifest loss.

In the fourth verse [70], His words: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning the signs indicating the oneness of Allah, the truth of His messengers and the soundness of their call, just as our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) came to you, O hypocrites, with clear proofs, and you denied as those before you denied, so the punishment of Allah descended upon them. The people of Noah were destroyed by the flood, 'Ad by the furious wind, Thamud by the thunderbolt, the people of Abraham by the removal of blessings and the arrival of afflictions, the companions of Madyan by the earthquake and the punishment of the darkness, and the overturned cities by rain. Al-iftikak means overturning, so that the upper parts of their three cities became their lower parts and their lower parts became their upper parts. Allah did not wrong them by what He sent down to them, but they wronged themselves. And you, O hypocrites, if you do not repent to your Lord, there will befall you what befell those before you, or worse, because you have not taken heed of what has passed.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Since the hypocrites' sickness is one, namely inner disbelief, their conduct is similar.

2- Enjoining wrong and forbidding right is a sign of hypocrisy, a manifestation of disbelief and an inversion of the natural disposition.

3- Being deluded by wealth and children is among the factors that prevent accepting the truth, submitting to it and yielding to it.

4- The similarity of human conditions and the following of some people by others in falsehood, corruption and evil.

5- The annulment of deeds through falsehood and the destruction of their doers is a decreed matter that does not fail.

6- The obligation to take lessons from the conditions of earlier peoples and to be warned by the punishment that disbelievers among them encountered.

5- The annulment of deeds through falsehood and the destruction of their doers is a decreed matter that does not fail.

6- The obligation to take lessons from the conditions of earlier peoples and to be warned by the punishment that disbelievers among them encountered.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 67–70:

Explanation of the words:

Al-munafiqun (the hypocrites): those who show the believers faith with their tongues while concealing disbelief in their hearts.

Ba'duhum min ba'd (some of them are from others): i.e., they are alike in their belief, their speech and their deeds, so their affair is one.

Bil-munkar (what is forbidden): i.e., what the Sharia denies because of its harm or ugliness, which is disbelief in Allah and His Messenger.

'An al-ma'ruf (what is good): i.e., what the Sharia recognizes as beneficial and therefore commands, such as faith and righteous deeds.

Yaqbidun aydiyahum (they withhold their hands): i.e., they hold them back from spending in the way of Allah.

Nasu Allah fa-nasiyahum (they forgot Allah, so He forgot them): i.e., they abandoned Allah, so they did not believe in Him and His Messenger, and so He abandoned them and deprived them of His guidance and success.

'Adhab muqim (lasting punishment): i.e., enduring, which does not cease or perish.

Bi-khala-qihim (with their share): i.e., with their portion and lot of this world.

Wa-khadtum (and you immersed yourselves): i.e., in falsehood and vain talk.

Wal-mu'tafikat (the overturned cities): i.e., the places that were turned upside down, so their upper part became their lower part; they are three cities.

Bil-bayyinat (with clear proofs): the signs that indicate the truth of their messengers' mission to them.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to expose the hypocrites and clarify their characteristics, in the hope that they will repent. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another﴾, meaning they are like parts of a single thing, because their affair is one: they do not differ from one another in belief, speech or action. Allah then describes their state by saying: ﴿They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right﴾. This is evidence of their inversion and the corruption of their hearts and minds, since this is the opposite of what sensible people command. What is meant by the wrong they enjoin is disbelief and disobedience, and the right they forbid is faith in Allah and His Messenger and obedience to them. His words ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾ are a metaphor for holding back and not giving generously in spending in the way of Allah. His words ﴿They forgot Allah﴾ mean they did not believe in Him, did not believe in His Messenger, and did not obey Allah and His Messenger; ﴿so He forgot them﴾ means Allah left them deprived of all guidance, mercy and kindness. His words ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ confirm the meaning of ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾, for their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger is what deprived them of Allah's guidance, so they committed every kind of defiant disobedience and were the disobedient deserving of this description, namely defiance and immersion in it.

In verse [68], His words: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein; it is sufficient for them﴾, meaning it is enough for them as recompense, ﴿and Allah has cursed them, and they will have lasting punishment﴾, meaning enduring, which does not cease, perish or end. This verse contains the most severe warning for the people of hypocrisy and disbelief, for the Lord, the Exalted, threatens them with the fire of Hell, abiding therein, and with lasting punishment that will never leave them nor relent for a moment, forever and ever, after Allah has cursed them, distancing them and removing them from every mercy and good.

In the third verse [69], Allah commands His Messenger to say to the hypocrites who mock Allah, His signs and His Messenger: You, O hypocrites, are like those who were before you in being deluded by wealth and children, in disbelieving in Allah and denying His Messenger, until the punishment of Allah descended upon them and His custom of destroying them took its course. This is what the noble verse contains, when He says: ﴿Like those before you, who were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their share, and you have enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share﴾, meaning their portion that was decreed for them in this world, ﴿and you have immersed yourselves as they immersed﴾, meaning in falsehood, evil, disbelief and denial, ﴿like those who immersed﴾, meaning like their immersion, exactly alike, those who perished, ﴿their deeds became worthless in this world and the Hereafter﴾, meaning they vanished and were gone, and they gained nothing from them, ﴿and those are the losers﴾.

Since you, O hypocrites, follow their path in disbelief, denial and delusion by wealth and children, your fate will be like theirs, which is manifest loss.

In the fourth verse [70], His words: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning the signs indicating the oneness of Allah, the truth of His messengers and the soundness of their call, just as our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) came to you, O hypocrites, with clear proofs, and you denied as those before you denied, so the punishment of Allah descended upon them. The people of Noah were destroyed by the flood, 'Ad by the furious wind, Thamud by the thunderbolt, the people of Abraham by the removal of blessings and the arrival of afflictions, the companions of Madyan by the earthquake and the punishment of the darkness, and the overturned cities by rain. Al-iftikak means overturning, so that the upper parts of their three cities became their lower parts and their lower parts became their upper parts. Allah did not wrong them by what He sent down to them, but they wronged themselves. And you, O hypocrites, if you do not repent to your Lord, there will befall you what befell those before you, or worse, because you have not taken heed of what has passed.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Since the hypocrites' sickness is one, namely inner disbelief, their conduct is similar.

2- Enjoining wrong and forbidding right is a sign of hypocrisy, a manifestation of disbelief and an inversion of the natural disposition.

3- Being deluded by wealth and children is among the factors that prevent accepting the truth, submitting to it and yielding to it.

4- The similarity of human conditions and the following of some people by others in falsehood, corruption and evil.

5- The annulment of deeds through falsehood and the destruction of their doers is a decreed matter that does not fail.

6- The obligation to take lessons from the conditions of earlier peoples and to be warned by the punishment that disbelievers among them encountered.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 71–72:

Explanation of the words:

"And the believing men and believing women": i.e., those who are truthful in their faith in Allah, His Messenger, and the promise and threat of Allah.

"Are protectors of one another": i.e., some of them take charge of others in support, protection, love, and aid.

"They establish prayer": i.e., they perform it with humility, fulfilling its conditions, pillars, recommended acts, and etiquettes.

"And give zakah": i.e., they pay the zakah on their wealth, both the silent wealth such as dirhams, dinars, and crops (al-mu'ashshirat), and the apparent wealth such as livestock: camels, cattle, and sheep.

"In gardens of perpetual residence (jannat 'Adn)": i.e., a lasting abode from which they will neither leave nor be moved.

"And approval from Allah is greater": i.e., the approval of Allah that He bestows upon them is greater than every bliss in Paradise.

Meaning of the two verses:

In connection with the mention of the hypocrites, their conduct, and the end of their affair, Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the believers, their good conduct, and their happy destiny, saying: "And the believing men and believing women" — i.e., those who believe in Allah, His Messenger, His promise, and His threat — "are protectors of one another" — i.e., some of them befriend others in love, support, cooperation, and aid. "They enjoin what is right" (al-ma'ruf), which is what the Sharia recognizes as truth and good, including faith and righteous deeds, "and forbid what is wrong" (al-munkar), which is what the Sharia recognizes as falsehood, harm, and corruption, including polytheism and all other crimes. Thus the believing men and believing women are the opposite of the hypocritical men and women in this matter. And His saying, "They establish prayer and give zakah": the hypocrites do not come to prayer except lazily; they neglect it and do not establish it. "And they withhold their hands" — they do not spend. The believers obey Allah and His Messenger, while the hypocrites disobey Allah and His Messenger. The believers, Allah will surely have mercy on them, and the hypocrites, Allah will surely punish them. "Indeed, Allah is Almighty" — victorious, who will surely fulfill His promise and threat — "All-Wise" — who places everything in its fitting place, so He does not punish the believers and bless the hypocrites, but rather blesses the believers and punishes the hypocrites.

And His saying in the second verse [72]: "Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow" — i.e., through their palaces and trees — "wherein they will abide forever, and pleasant dwellings" — i.e., good palaces in the utmost cleanliness and fragrance — "in gardens of perpetual residence (Eden)" — i.e., a lasting abode. And His saying, "And approval from Allah" — i.e., which He bestows upon them — "is greater" than the gardens, the palaces, and all other kinds of bliss. And His saying, "That is the great achievement" — that mentioned Paradise and its bliss and the approval of Allah therein is the great achievement. Success (al-fawz) is safety from what is feared and attaining what is desired. This true divine promise to the believing men and believing women is contrasted with Allah's threat to the hypocrites and disbelievers in the preceding verses, whose text is: "Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide forever. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment" [verse 68].

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Explanation of the qualities of the believing men and believing women, which are the manifestations and evidences of their faith.

2- The importance of the qualities of the people of faith: mutual allegiance, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, establishing prayer, giving zakah, and obeying Allah and His Messenger.

3- Explanation of the reward of the people of faith in the Hereafter, which is everlasting bliss in the abode of Islam.

4- The superiority of Allah's approval over all other bliss.

5- Explanation of the meaning of success, which is salvation from the Fire and entry into Paradise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 73–74:

Explanation of the words:

Jahid al-kuffar (strive against the disbelievers): exert your utmost effort in fighting the disbelievers and the hypocrites.

Waghluz 'alayhim (and be harsh toward them): i.e., in speech and action; be severe with them and do not be lenient toward them.

Kalimat al-kufr (the word of disbelief): i.e., a word by which the one who says it becomes a disbeliever. It is the statement of al-Jallas ibn Suwayd: "If what Muhammad brings is true, then we are worse than donkeys."

Wa hammu bima lam yanalu (and they plotted what they could not attain): i.e., they plotted to kill the Prophet ﷺ in a base conspiracy while they were returning from Tabuk.

Wa ma naqamu illa an aghnahum (and they held against them nothing except that He enriched them): i.e., they disliked or denounced nothing in Islam or its Messenger except that Allah enriched them after poverty. Is there anything to hold against this? They plot to kill the Messenger of Allah?

Meaning of the two verses:

The Most High commands His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾. Striving against the disbelievers is by the sword, and striving against the hypocrites is by the tongue. His words ﴿and be harsh with them﴾ mean: intensify your action and your speech. There is no leniency toward one who disbelieves in Allah and His Messenger, nor toward one who is a hypocrite toward the Messenger and the believers, who shows faith and conceals disbelief. His words ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and what an evil destination﴾ mean: Hell. He wills that you exert whatever you can in fighting them, by killing and disciplining. This is their portion in this world, and in the Hereafter their refuge is Hell, and what an evil destination.

His words in the second verse [74]: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they had certainly said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam, and they plotted what they could not attain﴾. This statement is the reason for the command to fight them and to be harsh with them, because of the statement of al-Jallas ibn Suwayd the hypocrite: "If what Muhammad brings is true, then we are worse than donkeys." A believer heard it from him and reported it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Jallas came making excuses and swearing by Allah that he had not said what he said, so Allah refuted him in His words in this verse: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they had certainly said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam﴾. The context indicates that such a wicked statement was repeated, and so it was.

As for His words ﴿and they plotted what they could not attain﴾, this refers to the hypocrites who conspired to kill the Prophet ﷺ upon his return from Tabuk, at the steep path on the way. But Allah exposed them, frustrated their scheme, and saved His Messenger from them, when He sent Ammar ibn Yasir to strike the faces of the mounts when they surrounded him. So they turned back and dispersed, after having resolved to jostle the Messenger of Allah with their camels while he was on his she-camel, so that he would fall from it and perish. Allah destroyed them.

His words ﴿and they held against them nothing﴾ mean: they disliked nothing about the Messenger of Allah or about Islam, except that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. Is enrichment after poverty something to be held against? The answer is no. Rather, it is disbelief and hypocrisy that corrupt taste, nature, and reason as well.

Despite what they committed of disbelief, evil, and corruption, the Lord, Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted, opens the door of repentance before them, and says: ﴿So if they repent﴾ from this disbelief, hypocrisy, evil, and corruption, ﴿it will be better for them﴾ in state and outcome, i.e., in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿But if they turn away﴾ from this offer, refuse it, and persist in disbelief and hypocrisy, ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, i.e., a painful one in this world through killing and disgrace, and in the Hereafter through the punishment of the Fire. ﴿And they will have no protector on earth﴾ who would take charge of them, nor a helper who would support them, i.e., they have no protector in this world who could ward off from them what Allah wills to send down upon them of disgrace and punishment, nor any helper to support them after Allah, the Most High, forsakes them.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The explanation of the verse of the sword, which is ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾.

2- Establishing the principle of apostasy (ridda), namely that a Muslim says a word of disbelief and thereby becomes a disbeliever, such as disparaging Islam, cursing Allah or His Messenger ﷺ, or denying what Allah has commanded to be believed and affirming its opposite, i.e., affirming what Allah has commanded to be denied.

3- Establishing the principle of repentance from all sins, and that whoever repents, his repentance is accepted.

4- A severe warning for whoever persists in disbelief and dies upon it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 75–78:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa minhum* (And among them): i.e., among the hypocrites (munafiqun).

*La-in atana min fadlihi* (If He gives us of His bounty): i.e., a great deal of wealth.

*Bakhilu bihi* (They were stingy with it): i.e., they withheld it and did not render its due, such as zakat (obligatory almsgiving) and other than it.

*Fa-a'qabahum nifaqan* (So He caused them to follow it with hypocrisy): i.e., their stinginess brought about hypocrisy that clung to their hearts, never leaving them until the day they meet Allah, exalted is He.

*Bima akhlafu Allah* (For having broken their promise to Allah): i.e., because of their breaking what they had promised Allah, exalted is He.

*Sirrahum wa najwahum* (Their secrets and their private consultations): i.e., what they conceal and hide within themselves, and what they confer about among themselves.

*Allam al-ghuyub* (Knower of the unseen): He knows every unseen thing on earth or in the heavens.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues concerning the hypocrites, who are of several categories, and this is another category among them. They made a covenant with Allah, the Exalted, that if He enriched them from His bounty and they became possessors of wealth and abundant property, they would surely give charity from it and would surely spend it in the paths of righteousness and goodness. But when Allah gave them what they asked and their wealth increased, they grew miserly and stingy with it, turned away from what they had pledged and from the piety and righteousness they had been upon, while they were averse. This stinginess and the breaking of promises and lying caused them to inherit *"hypocrisy in their hearts"* that does not leave them until they meet their Lord. This is what is indicated by the words of the Exalted: *"And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: 'If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous.' But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away while they were averse. So He caused them to follow it with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to Allah and because they used to lie."* (9:75–77)

As for the last verse [78], which is the words of the Exalted: *"Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private consultations, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?"* It contains a rebuke from Allah, the Exalted, to the hypocrites who made a covenant with Allah and broke it with their shameful conduct, as if they did not know that Allah knows their secrets and private consultations and that He, the Exalted, is the Knower of the unseen. Otherwise, how would they promise Him and swear to Him? Or do they think that Allah does not hear their secrets and private consultations? Their conduct is therefore a disgraceful and shameful position for them. Woe to them, since the fruit of it, which is hypocrisy, has clung to them until death, and by this the door of repentance was closed in their faces, and they perished with those who perish.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation to fulfill covenants, especially the covenants of Allah.

2- The condemnation of stinginess and its people.

3- Establishing the principle that an evil deed gives birth to another evil deed.

4- The permissibility of rebuking and reprimanding the people of falsehood.

5- The obligation of being mindful of Allah, for if these hypocrites had been mindful of Allah, they would not have departed from His obedience.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 79–80:

Explanation of the words:

Yalmizun (yalmizūn): that is, they find fault with and disparage.

Al-muṭṭawwi'in (al-muṭṭawwiʿīn): that is, those who give charity from their wealth beyond what is obligatory.

Illā juhdahum (illā juhdahum): except their capacity, and what they are able to do and so bring.

Fayaskharūna minhum (fa-yaskharūna minhum): that is, they mock them, belittling them.

Istaghfir lahum (istaghfir lahum): that is, ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask.

Lā yahdī al-qawm al-fāsiqīn (lā yahdī al-qawm al-fāsiqīn): that is, He does not guide them to what is good for them and their happiness, because of their deep immersion in disobedience.

Meaning of the two verses:

The context continues in condemning the hypocrites and exposing their deceit. Allah, the Exalted, informed that ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers regarding charity, and those who find nothing but their effort, so they mock them—Allah will mock them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ He informed that He mocks them in recompense for their mockery of the charitable, and He threatened them with a painful punishment. The manner of their faultfinding against the volunteers was that the Prophet ﷺ called for charity; when a man brought a large amount of wealth, they found fault with him and said, "He is showing off," and when a man brought a little, they found fault with him and said, "Allah is not in need of this sā' of yours." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse concerning them, exposing them, mocking them, and threatening them with painful punishment. He informed His Prophet that asking forgiveness for them and not asking it are equal, saying: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾, and He explained the cause of that in His saying: ﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾. This cause is sufficient for their not being forgiven, because it is disbelief, and the disbeliever is eternal in the Fire. Allah, the Exalted, also informed that He has deprived them of guidance, so they do not repent, saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾, because defiance has become a fixed attribute of theirs; therefore they do not repent, and by that they were deprived of the guidance of Allah, the Exalted.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of defaming and disparaging the believer.

2- The prohibition of mocking the believer.

3- Allah's jealousy for His friends, as He mocked those who mocked the charitable.

4- Whoever dies in disbelief, asking forgiveness for him does not benefit him; rather, it is not permissible to ask forgiveness for him.

5- Deep immersion in defiance, disbelief, or wrongdoing deprives its possessor of guidance.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 81–83:

Explanation of the words:

*Farija al-mukhallafun* (فرح المخلفون): i.e., those who stayed behind from jihad with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were delighted.

*Wa qalu: la tanfiru fi al-harr* (وقالوا: لا تنفروا في الحر): i.e., the hypocrites said to one another, "Do not go out to fight in the heat."

*Law kanu yafqahun* (لو كانوا يفقهون): i.e., if they understood the secrets of matters, their consequences and their outcomes, they would not have said, "Do not go out in the heat," but they do not understand.

*Fal-yadhhaku qalilan wa-liyabku kathiran* (فليضحكوا قليلاً وليبكوا): i.e., in this world, and let them weep much in the Hereafter.

*Fa-in rajaaka Allahu ila ta'ifatin minhum* (فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم): i.e., of the hypocrites.

*Fa-uq'udu ma'a al-khalifin* (فاقعدوا مع الخالفين): i.e., those who stayed behind from Tabuk, among the women, the children and those with excuses.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak about the hypocrites, and Allah, the Exalted, says, reporting about them: ﴿Those who stayed behind rejoiced in their sitting [at home] contrary to the Messenger of Allah﴾, i.e., the ones who stayed behind were glad to remain sitting in Madinah after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [had left], ﴿and they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾. Their dislike of jihad was the fruit of their hypocrisy and disbelief, and their saying ﴿Do not go out in the heat.﴾ For the Battle of Tabuk took place in intense heat. They said this to one another, and here Allah commanded His Messenger to answer their saying: ﴿Say: The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat.﴾ So why do they not guard themselves against it by going out in the cause of Allah, just as they guard themselves against the heat by not going out? His saying, ﴿if they only understood﴾, i.e., they would not have stayed behind from jihad, since the Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, ﴿but they do not understand.﴾ And His saying, ﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾, i.e., in this worldly life, with the joys that come to them, and let them weep much on the Day of Resurrection because of the deprivation and punishment that will befall them, ﴿as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾ of evil and corruption. And His saying to His Messenger ﷺ, ﴿So if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾, i.e., if Allah brings you back safely from Tabuk to Madinah to a group of the hypocrites, ﴿and they ask your permission to go out [with you]﴾ to a raid or a jihad, ﴿then say: Never shall you go out with me, and never shall you fight an enemy with me.﴾ The reason for this is: ﴿Indeed you were content with sitting [at home] the first time, so sit [now] with those who stay behind.﴾ i.e., among the women and children. For this increases their grief and magnifies their regret, as a recompense for their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah and their dislike of jihad with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Among the signs of hypocrisy is rejoicing at abandoning the obedience of Allah and His Messenger.

2- Among the signs of hypocrisy is disliking obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

3- Disapproval of excessive laughter.

4- Deliberately abandoning obedience may cause one to be deprived of it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 84–85:

Explanation of the words:

"And never pray over any of them who has died": i.e., the funeral prayer (salat al-janazah).

"Nor stand at his grave": i.e., do not take charge of his burial and supplication for him as you do with the believers.

"And they died while they were defiant": i.e., they departed from the obedience of Allah and His Messenger.

"And their souls will depart while they are disbelievers": i.e., their souls will leave their bodies at death while they are disbelievers.

The meaning of the two verses:

The context still concerns the hypocrites who remained behind from the expedition of Tabuk, although this verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the chief of the hypocrites. When he died, his son al-Hubab, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had named 'Abd Allah, and who said to him, "Hubab is the name of Satan," came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father has died, so give me your shirt to shroud him in, seeking its blessing, and pray over him and ask forgiveness for him, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him the shirt and said, "When you have finished, inform me." When he wanted to pray over him, 'Umar seized him and said, "Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?" He said, "No, rather He gave me the choice," and he said, "Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them." So he prayed over him, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And never pray over any of them who has died, nor stand at his grave﴾, i.e., do not take charge of his burial or supplicate for him to be firm at the time of questioning. Allah, exalted, gave the reason for this ruling with His saying ﴿Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiant﴾, and His saying ﴿And let not their wealth or their children impress you﴾, so that you would pray over them. Indeed, I only give them these things not as honor for them, but so that I may punish them with them in this world through grief and worry, ﴿and their souls will depart while they are disbelievers﴾, i.e., they will die, ﴿and they are disbelievers﴾, so they will be transferred to an everlasting punishment from which they will never leave, and that is the recompense of whoever disbelieves in Allah and His Messenger.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of praying over a disbeliever in all cases.

2- The prohibition of washing a disbeliever, standing at his burial, and supplicating for him.

3- The disliking of praying over people of corruption (fisq) short of disbelief.

4- The prohibition of being impressed by the material circumstances of disbelievers.
