The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him the shirt and said, "When you have finished, inform me." When he wanted to pray over him, 'Umar seized him and said, "Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?" He said, "No, rather He gave me the choice," and he said, "Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them." So he prayed over him, and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And never pray over any of them who has died, nor stand at his grave﴾, i.e., do not take charge of his burial or supplicate for him to be firm at the time of questioning. Allah, exalted, gave the reason for this ruling with His saying ﴿Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiant﴾, and His saying ﴿And let not their wealth or their children impress you﴾, so that you would pray over them. Indeed, I only give them these things not as honor for them, but so that I may punish them with them in this world through grief and worry, ﴿and their souls will depart while they are disbelievers﴾, i.e., they will die, ﴿and they are disbelievers﴾, so they will be transferred to an everlasting punishment from which they will never leave, and that is the recompense of whoever disbelieves in Allah and His Messenger.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of praying over a disbeliever in all cases.

2- The prohibition of washing a disbeliever, standing at his burial, and supplicating for him.

3- The disliking of praying over people of corruption (fisq) short of disbelief.

4- The prohibition of being impressed by the material circumstances of disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 86–90:

Explanation of the words:

Yasta'dhinuka: that is, they asked your permission to stay behind.

Ulu al-tawl minhum: that is, the wealthy and the affluent among them.

Dharna nakun ma'a al-qa'idin: that is, leave us with those who stay behind: the infirm, the sick, the children and the women.

Ma'a al-khawalif: that is, with the women. Khawalif is the plural of khalifa, the woman who remains behind in the house when the man is absent.

Tuba'a 'ala qulubihim: that is, their sins followed one upon another on their hearts until they became a seal upon them, and so knowledge was veiled from them.

Lahum al-khayrat: that is, in this world, through victory and spoils, and in the Hereafter, through Paradise and its honour therein.

Wa-ula'ika hum al-mufliḥun: that is, those who succeed by being safe from what is feared and by attaining what is loved.

Al-mu'adhdhirun: that is, those who make excuses.

Wa qa'ada alladhina kadhabu Allah: that is, and those who lied to God did not come to seek permission to sit out the jihad; they were the hypocrite Bedouins.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to expose the faults of the hypocrites and to clarify their conditions. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when a surah is sent down﴾, that is, a portion of the Qur'an, one verse or several verses, ﴿saying: "Believe in God and strive alongside His Messenger"﴾, that is, it commands belief in God and jihad alongside His Messenger, ﴿the men of wealth among them ask your permission﴾, that is, among the hypocrites, ﴿and say: "Leave us, that we may be with those who sit behind."﴾, that is, those who stay behind from jihad due to incapacity, such as the sick, the women and the children. God said, in reproach and rebuke of them: ﴿They are content to be with the women who remain behind﴾, that is, with the women, and that is due to their cowardice and psychological defeat. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and a seal was set upon their hearts﴾, that is, God sealed their hearts with the traces of their sins, which had covered their hearts; therefore they do not understand the meaning of the speech. Otherwise they would not have been content with the stigma of shame, which is to be in the houses with the women. This is the state of the hypocrites and these are their disgraces: when a surah is sent down commanding belief and jihad, they come without modesty or dignity, asking permission to remain with the women. ﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their selves﴾, and they did not ask permission, so they won the honour of this world and the Hereafter. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those—for them are the good things﴾, that is, in this world through victories and spoils, and in the Hereafter through Paradise, its delights and the good pleasure of God therein. And He said: ﴿And those—they are the successful﴾, that is, those who succeed by being safe from every feared thing and by attaining every desired thing. God, exalted is He, explained those good things and that success in His saying in verse [89]: ﴿God has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever.﴾ And He informed about what He has prepared for them of that lasting bliss, that it is the triumph, saying: ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾ This is what the four verses indicate. As for the fifth verse [90], it includes God's informing about the hypocrites among the Bedouins, that is, the desert dwellers. Therefore God said of them: ﴿There will afflict those among them who disbelieved a painful punishment﴾, in this world and in the Hereafter, if they die upon their disbelief.

1- The Qur'an is the first source of divine legislation and the Sunnah is the second.

2- The permissibility of seeking permission out of pressing need.

3- The prohibition of seeking permission to stay behind from jihad when one is able to perform it.

4- The prohibition of staying behind from jihad without permission from the Imam.

5- The virtue of jihad with wealth and self in the way of God.

6- The explanation of the great reward and abundant recompense for the people of faith and jihad.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 9, verses 91–92:

Explanation of the words:

"Upon the weak": that is, such as the elderly. "Nor upon the sick": such as the blind and the lame.

"Blame" (haraj): that is, sin for staying behind.

"When they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger": that is, there is no blame upon them for staying behind when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger, and this is by their obedience to Allah and His Messenger together with their abandoning of spreading false rumours (irjaf) and discouraging others (tathbit).

"There is no way against the good-doers": that is, no path to taking them to account.

"To provide them with mounts": that is, on riding beasts they could mount.

"They turned back": that is, they returned to their homes.

"Their eyes overflowing with tears": that is, flowing with abundant tears out of grief at not being able to go out.

The meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, censured those who stayed behind and threatened with a painful punishment those among them who did not offer an excuse, He mentioned in these verses that there is no blame upon those who have valid excuses, namely the weak, such as the elderly, the sick, the blind, the lame, and the poor who cannot find what to spend, but on the condition that they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. So He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾, meaning there is no sin, ﴿when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾. The meaning of sincerity to Allah and His Messenger is obeying them in commands and prohibitions, abandoning spreading false rumours, discouraging others, and opposing propaganda against Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and striving in the cause of Allah. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿There is no way against the good-doers﴾, means there is no path against those who did good in their staying behind, because first, they have a lawful excuse; second, they are obedient to Allah and His Messenger; and third, their hearts and faces are with Allah and His Messenger, and even if their bodies stayed behind due to the excuse, there is no path for anyone to belittle them or harm them in any way. Likewise there is no path ﴿against those who, when they came to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾ for jihad with you on your march, and you said, apologising to them, ﴿I cannot find anything to mount you on﴾, and they turned back, returning to their dwellings weeping, with tears overflowing from their eyes in grief, ﴿because they could not find what to spend﴾ on their march with you. They were a group of men among whom were al-Irbad ibn Sariyah and the sons of Muqarrin, who were a clan of Muzayna, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Guidance from the two verses:

1. There is no blame upon those with excuses, whom Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ [al-Nur: 61], and in this verse: ﴿nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾, provided they obey Allah and the Messenger in what they are able to do, and are sincere to Allah and His Messenger by word and deed, and abstain from discouraging, demoralising and spreading rumours opposed to Islam and the Muslims.

2. Manifestations of the Muhammadan perfection in his humility, mercy, kindness and benevolence towards the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 9, verses 91–92:

Explanation of the words:

"Upon the weak": that is, such as the elderly. "Nor upon the sick": such as the blind and the lame.

"Blame" (haraj): that is, sin for staying behind.

"When they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger": that is, there is no blame upon them for staying behind when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger, and this is by their obedience to Allah and His Messenger together with their abandoning of spreading false rumours (irjaf) and discouraging others (tathbit).

"There is no way against the good-doers": that is, no path to taking them to account.

"To provide them with mounts": that is, on riding beasts they could mount.

"They turned back": that is, they returned to their homes.

"Their eyes overflowing with tears": that is, flowing with abundant tears out of grief at not being able to go out.

The meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, censured those who stayed behind and threatened with a painful punishment those among them who did not offer an excuse, He mentioned in these verses that there is no blame upon those who have valid excuses, namely the weak, such as the elderly, the sick, the blind, the lame, and the poor who cannot find what to spend, but on the condition that they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. 1. There is no blame upon those with excuses, whom Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ [al-Nur: 61], and in this verse: ﴿nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾, provided they obey Allah and the Messenger in what they are able to do, and are sincere to Allah and His Messenger by word and deed, and abstain from discouraging, demoralising and spreading rumours opposed to Islam and the Muslims.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 9, Verses 93–96**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Innama al-sabil* (the way): i.e., the path to punishment.

*Aghniya'* (the wealthy): those who have the means for jihad while their bodies are sound.

*Al-khawalif* (those left behind): i.e., the women, the children, and the infirm.

*Idha raja'tum ilayhim* (when you return to them): i.e., when you come back to them from Tabuk. They were some eighty-odd men.

*Lan nu'mina lakum* (we will not believe you): i.e., we will not accept what you say as true.

*Thumma turaddun* (then you will be returned): i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

*Idha inqalabtum* (when you have returned): i.e., when you came back from Tabuk.

*Li-tu'ridu 'anhum* (that you may turn away from them): i.e., that you not punish them.

*Rijs* (impurity): i.e., filth, because of the corruption of their inner selves.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues concerning those left behind, both hypocrites and non-hypocrites. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿The only way (of blame) is against those who ask your permission while they are wealthy and able to spend and to travel.﴾ That is, the path to punishing those left behind is against those who ask you for exemption from the expedition while they are wealthy, capable of spending and travelling. ﴿They are content to be with the women who are left behind.﴾ That is, with the women. ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts⁠﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿—⁠﻿﻿—﻿ because of their sins, so they do not know that their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah will not benefit them, and that it will bring upon them a trial they cannot bear.﴾ These are the ones against whom you have a path for punishing and holding them accountable, not those who cannot find what to spend and who asked you for mounts, but you could not find anything to carry them, so they returned to their homes weeping with grief. This is what the first verse [93] indicates.

As for the three verses after it, they concern the hypocrites among those left behind. Allah, the Exalted, informs about them, saying: ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them.﴾ They will seek your pardon when you return to Madinah from your expedition. Say to them, O our Messenger: ﴿Do not make excuses, for we will not believe you⁠﻿﻿—﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿—﻿ that is, we will not accept what you say, because Allah, the Exalted, has informed us of your news. ﴿Allah will see your deeds and His Messenger.﴾ Whether you repent and sincerely devote your religion to Allah, or you persist in your disbelief and hypocrisy, ﴿you will be returned after your death to the realm of the unseen and the witnessed,﴾ which is Allah, the Exalted, and He will inform you on the Day of Resurrection after your resurrection of what you used to do, of good deeds or evil deeds, and will recompense you with that just recompense.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may turn away from them,﴾ Allah, the Exalted, informs His Messenger and the believers, saying: these left-behind ones will swear to you when you return to them, that is, to Madinah, so that you will turn away from them. So turn away from them, that is, do not hold them accountable and do not pay attention to them. ﴿Indeed, they are impurity,﴾ that is, filth, ﴿and their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn of disbelief, hypocrisy, and sins.﴾ As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They swear to you⁠﻿—﻿﻿—﻿ offering excuses of various kinds so that you will be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, their pleasure will not benefit them at all, because they are defiantly disobedient, and Allah does not be pleased with the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ And as long as He is not pleased with them, He is angry with them, and whoever Allah is angry with, He destroys and punishes. Therefore, your pleasure with them and your lack of it are equal.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. There is no path to harming sincere believers who stay behind, for they stayed behind only out of a valid excuse. The path (of blame) lies only against the wealthy, who are able to march to jihad, yet sat back from it because of their hypocrisy.

2. Making excuses is permissible, on condition that the person is truthful in his excuse.

3. The hypocrites are like the polytheists: they are impurity, that is, filth, because their inner selves are corrupt with polytheism and disbelief, and their hidden deeds are also corrupt, since all of them are plotting against the Muslims, deceiving them, and scheming against them.

4. It is forbidden to be pleased with a defiant sinner who openly flaunts his sin, since he must be hated. How then can one be pleased with him and love him?

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 97–99:

Explanation of the words:

Al-A'rab (the Bedouins): plural of a'rabi, meaning one who dwells in the desert (al-badiyah).

Ashaddu kufran wa nifaqan (more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy): i.e., more than the disbelievers and hypocrites of the settled towns (al-hadarah).

Wa ajdar (and more fitting): i.e., more deserving and more entitled.

Hudud ma anzala Allah (the limits of what God has sent down): i.e., the laws of Islam.

Maghraman (a burden): i.e., a penalty and a loss.

Yatarabbas (he waits): i.e., he awaits.

Al-dawa'ir (the misfortunes): plural of da'irah, meaning any calamity or disaster that surrounds a person.

Da'irat al-su' (the evil turn of fortune): i.e., the calamity that grieves them and does not gladden them, namely destruction.

Qurubat (means of nearness): plural of qurbah, meaning a praiseworthy station.

Wa salawat al-Rasul (and the prayers of the Messenger): i.e., his supplication for them for good.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to expose the hypocrites and prepare them either for repentance or for their destruction. In the first verse [97], God, exalted is He, informs that the Bedouins, who are the inhabitants of the desert among the Arabs, are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy than the disbelievers and hypocrites of the settled towns. And they are more fitting, i.e., more likely and more entitled, not to know the limits of what God has sent down to His Messenger, i.e., the rulings and sunnahs, and that is because of their distance from contact with the people of the settled towns. The words of God, exalted is He, ﴿And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, mean: All-Knowing of His creation, All-Wise in His legislation. So what He informs of is the truth that has occurred, and what He decrees is the justice that is obligatory.

His words, exalted is He, in the second verse [98]: ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who takes what he spends as a burden﴾, mean: among some of the Bedouins is one who considers what he spends in jihad to be a penalty imposed upon him and a loss that befalls him in his wealth. That is because he does not believe in the reward and punishment of the Hereafter, being a disbeliever in God and in the meeting with God, exalted is He. His words, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿And he waits for misfortunes to befall you﴾, mean: he awaits for you, O Muslims, the misfortunes, when they will descend upon you, so that he may be rid of you and of spending on you. The dawa'ir are the plural of da'irah, the calamity and the event that descends from occurrences. His words, exalted is He, ﴿Upon them is the evil turn of fortune﴾: this sentence is a supplication against them, a recompense for what they await for the believers. His words, ﴿And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, mean: All-Hearing of their statements, All-Knowing of their intentions, so He has supplicated against them with what they deserve.

His words, exalted is He, in the third verse [99]: ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who believes in God and the Last Day and takes what he spends as means of nearness to God and as the prayers of the Messenger﴾. This is an information from Him, exalted is He, that the Bedouins are not all alike, but among them is one who believes in God and the Last Day; therefore he takes what he spends in jihad as means of nearness to God, i.e., a nearness by which he draws close to God, exalted is He, and as a means to obtain the supplication of the Messenger for him, because the Messenger ﷺ, when a believer came to him with his zakat or charity, would supplicate for him with good, as in his saying to Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa: "O God, send blessings upon the family of Abi Awfa." His words, exalted is He, ﴿Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them﴾, are an information from Him, exalted is He, that He has accepted it from them and it has become a means of nearness for them with Him, exalted is He. His words, exalted is He, ﴿God will admit them into His mercy﴾, are a glad tidings to them of entry into Paradise. His words, ﴿Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾, confirm God's promise to them of admitting them into His mercy, which is Paradise, for He forgives their sins first and admits them into Paradise second. This is His, exalted is He, way with His friends: He purifies them, then bestows His favour upon them with His nearness.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that the inhabitants of the desert are deprived of many manners and knowledge, so dwelling in the desert is not praiseworthy unless it is a flight from trials.

2- Among the Bedouins are the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the pious, the disobedient and the wicked, just as among the inhabitants of cities; however, the disbelievers and hypocrites of the desert are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy because of the influence of the environment.

3- The virtue of spending in the way of God and sincerity in it for God, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 100–102:

Explanation of the words:

"And the foremost (al-sabiqun)": that is, in faith, emigration, support and jihad.

"Followed them with excellence": that is, in their righteous deeds.

"Allah is pleased with them": because of their obedience to Him, their turning back to Him, their fear of Him and their desire for what is with Him.

"And they are pleased with Him": for what He has bestowed upon them of magnificent blessings and great favours.

"And among those around you": that is, around Madinah, among the tribes of the Arabs.

"They have become accustomed (marradu)": they became skilled in it and persisted in it, and were defiant in it.

"We will punish them twice": the first may be their disgrace among the Muslims, and the second the punishment of the grave.

The meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And the foremost, the first of the emigrants and the helpers﴾: these are those who preceded others to faith, emigration, support and jihad, and those who followed them in that and perfected their deeds, so that they were in accordance with what Allah legislated and what His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) explained. All of them, Allah is pleased with them for their faith and righteous deeds, and they are pleased with Him for the favour and honour He granted them. He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is, give them the good news of what He has prepared for them of gardens. And His saying ﴿That is the great triumph﴾: that is, that mentioned — His pleasure with them, their pleasure with Him, and the preparation of Paradise for them — is the great triumph. Triumph is safety from what is feared and attaining what is desired; so deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise is the great triumph. This is what the first verse [100] indicates.

As for the second verse, it contains the information that there are hypocrites among the Bedouins around Madinah, and hypocrites within Madinah itself; however, because of their skill and persistence in hypocrisy, they have come to be unrecognised. But Allah, may He be exalted, knows them. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have become accustomed to hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them﴾. And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾ is a threat against them that is certain to be carried out, namely that He, may He be exalted, will punish them in this world twice: once by exposing them, or by whatever punishment He wills, and once in their graves. Then, after the Resurrection, He will return them to the punishment of the Fire, which is the great punishment.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in the second verse [102]: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾: these are other people who stayed behind from jihad without excuse, namely Abu Lubabah and a group with him of six or seven men, who tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque when they heard what was revealed concerning those who stayed behind, and said, "We will not untie ourselves until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) unties us." They mixed a righteous deed, which was their faith, jihad and Islam, with an evil deed, which was their staying behind from the expedition of Tabuk without excuse. So His saying ﴿It may be that Allah will accept their repentance﴾ is an announcement to them of Allah's acceptance of their repentance. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and untied them, and they said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "This is our wealth that caused us to stay behind from you; take it, give it in charity, and ask forgiveness for us." He said, "I have not been commanded to take anything of your wealth."

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of precedence in good and the attainment of priority in it.

2- The virtue of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over those who came after them.

3- The virtue of the Successors (tabi'un) to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) if they follow them well.

4- Knowledge of what is in hearts belongs to Allah the Exalted; no one knows of the unseen except what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has taught.

5- Hope for the people of tawhid who mixed a righteous deed with another evil one, that Allah will forgive them and have mercy on them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 103–106:

Explanation of the words:

Sadaqah (ṣadaqah): wealth by which one draws near to Allah, the Exalted.

Tutahhiruhum wa-tuzakkihim biha (you purify them and cause them to grow in goodness through it): i.e., you purify them from their sins, and you, O Messenger, cause them to grow in goodness through it by your supplication for them and your praise of them.

Wa-ṣalli 'alayhim (and pray for them): i.e., supplicate for them good.

Inna ṣalataka sakanun lahum (indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them): i.e., your supplication is a mercy.

Wa-yaʼkhudhu al-ṣadaqat (and He takes the charities): He accepts them.

Murjawna li-amri Allah (deferred to the command of Allah): deferred to the judgement and decree of Allah.

ʻAlim ḥakim (All-Knowing, All-Wise): i.e., knowing of His creation's intentions, wealth and deeds, wise in His decree and His legislation.

Meaning of the verses:

Earlier, in the verse before these, it was mentioned that the disobedient repentant ones said to the Messenger ﷺ: "These are our wealth, because of which we stayed behind; take it, O Messenger of Allah." He said to them: "I have not been commanded to do that." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ So Allah, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger to take the charity of these repentant ones, because it purifies them from their sins and from the filth of miserliness in their souls, and causes them to grow, O Messenger, through your acceptance of it. "And pray for them" means supplicate for them with good. "Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them" means mercy and tranquillity in their souls. "And Allah is Hearing" of their words when they presented their charity and said, "Take it, O Messenger of Allah"; "Knowing" of their intentions and the impulses of their souls, for they are truly and sincerely repentant.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants﴾, the interrogative is for affirmation, meaning they know this with certainty. "And takes the charities" means He accepts them. "And that Allah is the Accepter of repentance" means He frequently accepts the repentance of those who repent, "the Merciful" to His believing servants. Then Allah, the Exalted, commanded His Messenger to say to them, urging them toward righteous deeds, as a purification and growth for their souls: ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers."﴾ That is, He will thank you for them and praise you for them. ﴿And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, and will recompense you for it: good for good and evil by its like.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah; either He will punish them or He will accept their repentance﴾, this is the third category of those who stayed behind. The first were the hypocrites, the second were the repentant ones, and the third is the subject of this verse. They were three men: Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayyah. These did not come to the Messenger ﷺ to apologise to him as the repentant ones who gave their wealth in charity did. Among them was Abu Lubabah, who tied himself to the pillars of the mosque, so the Messenger ﷺ ordered that they be shunned until Allah judges concerning them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿deferred to the command of Allah; either He will punish them or He will accept their repentance. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ So whether He punishes them or accepts their repentance, that is by His knowledge and wisdom. They remained in that state until the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls became constricted for them. Then Allah, the Exalted, accepted their repentance, as came after several verses at the end of this surah: ﴿And that Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- Charity expiates sins and purifies souls from the vice of miserliness and stinginess.

2- It is recommended for one who receives the charity of a Muslim to supplicate for him with such words as: "May Allah reward you for what you gave, and bless you in what you have kept."

3- It is incumbent upon one who repents from a major sin to increase afterward in righteous deeds, such as charity, prayer, and the like.

4- The virtue of fear and hope: fear impels one to abandon sins, and hope impels one to increase in righteous deeds.

The meaning of the verses

The context continues to expose the hypocrites and close the doors of hypocrisy in their faces, until they repent to God Most High or perish while disbelievers. So God Most High said, mentioning a group of them: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as an ambush for whoever had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾. The intended ones who took a mosque for harm and disbelief were twelve men from the people of Madinah who came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was setting out for Tabuk and said, "O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for the weak among us and the sick and for the rainy night, so pray for us in it." He ﷺ said to them, "I am now on the point of a journey, and if we return we will pray for you in it, God willing, or as he said." When the Prophet ﷺ returned from Tabuk and reached a place near Madinah called Dhu Awan, which is an hour's distance from Madinah, revelation came down concerning the Mosque of Harm. So he sent Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of Banū Sālim ibn 'Awf, and Ma'n ibn 'Adī, or his brother 'Āṣim, brother of Banū al-'Ajlān, and said, "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, and demolish it and burn it." So they went out hastily until they reached Banū Sālim ibn 'Awf, who were the kin of Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum. He said to Ma'n, "Wait for me until I bring you fire," so he came out with palm fronds that had been set alight, and the two of them went to the mosque while its people were in it, and they set it on fire and demolished it, and its people scattered. There was revealed concerning them the saying of God Most High: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾, meaning for the purpose of harming the Prophet's Mosque and the Mosque of Qubā', until the people of the quarter came to them. His saying ﴿and disbelief﴾ means for the purpose of disbelief in God and His Messenger. His saying ﴿and division among the believers﴾ is a third cause for building the Mosque of Harm, since the people of the quarter were gathered in the Mosque of Qubā', so they wanted to split them between two mosques so that these hypocrites would find room for doubt and slander and for dividing the ranks of the believers, according to the principle: "divide and rule." ﴿and as an ambush for whoever had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾, and this is Abū 'Āmir the monk, the wicked one, for he, may God's curses be upon him, is the one who ordered them to build it so that it would be a den for conspiracy and plotting. This wicked man said to the Prophet ﷺ, "I have not found a people who fight you except that I fight you with them." So he was with the polytheists in all their wars until the polytheists were defeated at Hawazin, and the accursed one despaired and went to the lands of Rome seeking their help against the Messenger of God ﷺ. From here he commanded the hypocrites to build the Mosque of Harm so that, as God Most High mentioned, he would arrive with it alongside the armies of Rome, whom he had gone out to seek and to incite. But he failed in his endeavour and perished in Syria, to Hell, and wretched is the destination. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿and as an ambush for whoever had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾, that is, before the building of the Mosque of Harm, which was demolished and burned, and became a place of refuse where carrion and filth were thrown.

His saying ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended only the good"﴾ is their words when the mosque was burned and demolished and their affair was exposed; they swore that they intended by building it nothing but a state that is good with no evil in it, for they said, "We built it for the sake of the sick and for the rainy night." His saying ﴿And God bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾ is a refutation of their words and an affirmation of their lying. His saying ﴿Do not stand in it ever﴾ is a prohibition to the Messenger ﷺ from praying for them in it, as he had promised them, while he was going to Tabuk. His saying ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it﴾ refers to his mosque ﷺ and the Mosque of Qubā', since each of them was founded from the first day upon piety from God and good pleasure, that is, upon fear of God and seeking His pleasure. His saying ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾ is praise of the people of Qubā' with good, and a report that they love to purify themselves from both sensory and moral impurity; they used to combine stones and water in istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself), so God Most High praised them for that. His saying ﴿Then is one who founded his building upon piety from God and good pleasure better, or one who founded his building upon the brink of a crumbling bank, that is, on the edge of a cliff overlooking collapse?﴾ The jurf is the ground at the edge of a valley which the torrent undermines from beneath, leaving the soil standing but overhanging collapse. His saying ﴿so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾ means that cliff fell with him into the fire of Hell, may God Most High protect us. This is the state of those hypocrites who built the Mosque of Harm. His saying ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means He does not guide them to that by which they would be perfected and made happy; that is, He deprives them of His guidance, so they lose in this world and the next. His saying ﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts﴾ means a doubt and turmoil in their souls ﴿unless their hearts are cut apart﴾, so that they perish; and the doubt in their hearts means that this wrongful building became a cause for the rooting of hypocrisy and disbelief in their hearts until they die as disbelievers. His saying ﴿And God is Knowing, Wise﴾ is a concluding remark confirming and establishing what has been said; His being Knowing and Wise entails depriving those wrongdoing hypocrites of guidance until they die as disbelievers, bound for Hell, because of their deep immersion in wrongdoing, polytheism and corruption.

2- Explanation that the contest for honour is the cause of all calamity. Ibn Ubayy fought Islam because he had hoped for rule over the people of Madinah, and Islam deprived him of it. Abū 'Āmir the monk took up monasticism for the sake of honour over the people of Madinah and spiritual authority; so when he lost it, he fought the one who had been the cause of his deprivation, the Messenger ﷺ, until he said to him face to face: "No people have fought you except that I fought you with them." 4- Any mosque built for harm and for dividing the Muslims must be demolished, and prayer in it is forbidden.

5- The virtue of purification and of going to excess in both the spiritual and bodily purities.

6- Warning against wrongdoing and excess in it, for it deprives its doer of God's guidance, so he perishes while a wrongdoer, losing in this world and the next.

The context continues to expose the hypocrites and close the doors of hypocrisy in their faces, until they repent to God Most High or perish while disbelievers. So God Most High said, mentioning a group of them: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as an ambush for whoever had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾. The intended ones who took a mosque for harm and disbelief were twelve men from the people of Madinah who came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was setting out for Tabuk and said, "O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for the weak among us and the sick and for the rainy night, so pray for us in it." He ﷺ said to them, "I am now on the point of a journey, and if we return we will pray for you in it, God willing, or as he said." When the Prophet ﷺ returned from Tabuk and reached a place near Madinah called Dhu Awan, which is an hour's distance from Madinah, revelation came down concerning the Mosque of Harm. So he sent Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of Banū Sālim ibn 'Awf, and Ma'n ibn 'Adī, or his brother 'Āṣim, brother of Banū al-'Ajlān, and said, "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, and demolish it and burn it." So they went out hastily until they reached Banū Sālim ibn 'Awf, who were the kin of Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum. He said to Ma'n, "Wait for me until I bring you fire," so he came out with palm fronds that had been set alight, and the two of them went to the mosque while its people were in it, and they set it on fire and demolished it, and its people scattered. There was revealed concerning them the saying of God Most High: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾, meaning for the purpose of harming the Prophet's Mosque and the Mosque of Qubā', until the people of the quarter came to them. His saying ﴿and disbelief﴾ means for the purpose of disbelief in God and His Messenger. His saying ﴿and division among the believers﴾ is a third cause for building the Mosque of Harm, since the people of the quarter were gathered in the Mosque of Qubā', so they wanted to split them between two mosques so that these hypocrites would find room for doubt and slander and for dividing the ranks of the believers, according to the principle: "divide and rule." ﴿and as an ambush for whoever had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾, and this is Abū 'Āmir the monk, the wicked one, for he, may God's curses be upon him, is the one who ordered them to build it so that it would be a den for conspiracy and plotting. This wicked man said to the Prophet ﷺ, "I have not found a people who fight you except that I fight you with them." So he was with the polytheists in all their wars until the polytheists were defeated at Hawazin, and the accursed one despaired and went to the lands of Rome seeking their help against the Messenger of God ﷺ. From here he commanded the hypocrites to build the Mosque of Harm so that, as God Most High mentioned, he would arrive with it alongside the armies of Rome, whom he had gone out to seek and to incite. But he failed in his endeavour and perished in Syria, to Hell, and wretched is the destination. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿and as an ambush for whoever had warred against God and His Messenger before﴾, that is, before the building of the Mosque of Harm, which was demolished and burned, and became a place of refuse where carrion and filth were thrown.

His saying ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended only the good"﴾ is their words when the mosque was burned and demolished and their affair was exposed; they swore that they intended by building it nothing but a state that is good with no evil in it, for they said, "We built it for the sake of the sick and for the rainy night." His saying ﴿And God bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾ is a refutation of their words and an affirmation of their lying. His saying ﴿Do not stand in it ever﴾ is a prohibition to the Messenger ﷺ from praying for them in it, as he had promised them, while he was going to Tabuk. His saying ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it﴾ refers to his mosque ﷺ and the Mosque of Qubā', since each of them was founded from the first day upon piety from God and good pleasure, that is, upon fear of God and seeking His pleasure. His saying ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾ is praise of the people of Qubā' with good, and a report that they love to purify themselves from both sensory and moral impurity; they used to combine stones and water in istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself), so God Most High praised them for that. His saying ﴿Then is one who founded his building upon piety from God and good pleasure better, or one who founded his building upon the brink of a crumbling bank, that is, on the edge of a cliff overlooking collapse?﴾ The jurf is the ground at the edge of a valley which the torrent undermines from beneath, leaving the soil standing but overhanging collapse. His saying ﴿so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾ means that cliff fell with him into the fire of Hell, may God Most High protect us. This is the state of those hypocrites who built the Mosque of Harm. His saying ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means He does not guide them to that by which they would be perfected and made happy; that is, He deprives them of His guidance, so they lose in this world and the next. His saying ﴿Their building which they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts﴾ means a doubt and turmoil in their souls ﴿unless their hearts are cut apart﴾, so that they perish; and the doubt in their hearts means that this wrongful building became a cause for the rooting of hypocrisy and disbelief in their hearts until they die as disbelievers. His saying ﴿And God is Knowing, Wise﴾ is a concluding remark confirming and establishing what has been said; His being Knowing and Wise entails depriving those wrongdoing hypocrites of guidance until they die as disbelievers, bound for Hell, because of their deep immersion in wrongdoing, polytheism and corruption.

Guidance from the verses

Among the guidance of the verses:

1- Explanation of the greatest conspiracy against Islam carried out by the hypocrites under the direction of the wicked monk Abū 'Āmir.

2- Explanation that the contest for honour is the cause of all calamity. Ibn Ubayy fought Islam because he had hoped for rule over the people of Madinah, and Islam deprived him of it. Abū 'Āmir the monk took up monasticism for the sake of honour over the people of Madinah and spiritual authority; so when he lost it, he fought the one who had been the cause of his deprivation, the Messenger ﷺ, until he said to him face to face: "No people have fought you except that I fought you with them." Indeed he went to Rome, inciting them against the Messenger of God ﷺ. And the Jews did not fight Islam except to preserve their hope of a kingdom of Israel.

3- It is not valid to be deceived by the words of the people of hypocrisy, for they are all lies.

4- Any mosque built for harm and for dividing the Muslims must be demolished, and prayer in it is forbidden.

5- The virtue of purification and of going to excess in both the spiritual and bodily purities.

6- Warning against wrongdoing and excess in it, for it deprives its doer of God's guidance, so he perishes while a wrongdoer, losing in this world and the next.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 111–112:

Explanation of the words:

Paradise (al-Jannah): It is the Abode of Peace (dar al-salam) which Allah the Exalted has prepared for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun).

They fight (yuqatilun): That is, the disbelievers and polytheists.

A promise (wa'dan): That is, He promised them a true promise.

In the Torah (fi al-Tawrah): That is, mentioned in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an.

And who is truer to his covenant (wa man awfa bi-'ahdihi): That is, no one is truer to his covenant than Allah the Exalted.

That is the great triumph (dhalika huwa al-fawz al-'azim): That is, that transaction is the great triumph.

The repentant (al-ta'ibun): That is, those who repent from polytheism, hypocrisy and sins.

The worshippers (al-'abidun): That is, those who obey Allah in humility and submission, together with their love for Allah and their glorification of Him.

The travellers (al-sa'ihun): That is, those who fast and those who go out in the way of Allah to seek knowledge, to teach it, or to wage jihad against His enemies.

Those who enjoin good (al-amirun bil-ma'ruf): That is, to worship Allah the Exalted and to affirm His Oneness in worship.

Those who forbid evil (al-nahunna 'an al-munkar): That is, from polytheism and sins.

And those who guard the limits of Allah (wa al-hafizun li-hudud Allah): That is, those who uphold them and act upon them.

And give good tidings to the believers (wa bashshir al-mu'minin): That is, of Paradise, the Abode of Peace.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted mentioned the state of those who stayed behind from jihad, He honoured jihad, encouraging it and what He has prepared for its people. So He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth, for that they will have Paradise﴾. This is the commodity for which Allah the Exalted gave the price, which is Paradise. His saying ﴿They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾ means: the enemies of Allah, the polytheists, are killed, and they are martyred in the battles of fighting. His saying ﴿a promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an﴾ means: He promised them this, and made it binding as a true promise, that is, He affirmed it in the three books, the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, as an affirmation and confirmation of it. His saying ﴿And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?﴾ is a rhetorical question meaning negation: no one at all is truer to his covenant when he makes a covenant than Allah the Exalted. His saying ﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have made with Him﴾ means: on the basis of that, rejoice, O believers, in your transaction which you have made with Allah the Exalted, that is, be glad and rejoice in it. That transaction and rejoicing is the great triumph, for which there is no better or greater triumph.

His saying ﴿The repentant...﴾ up to ﴿and those who guard the limits of Allah﴾ is a description of the attributes of the people of this transaction and a defining of them. They are described by nine attributes. The first: the repentant, that is, from polytheism and sins. The second: the worshippers, who are those who obey Allah with an obedience filled with love for Allah, glorification of Him and awe of Him. The third: those who praise Allah in prosperity and adversity and in every state. The fourth: the travellers, who are the fasters, as in the hadith, and those who go out in the way of Allah to seek knowledge, or to wage war, or to teach, or to call to Allah, so that He may be worshipped, made One, and obeyed in His commands and prohibitions. The fifth and sixth: those who bow and prostrate, that is, those who establish prayer and abound in its voluntary acts, as if they are always in bowing and prostration. The seventh and eighth: those who enjoin good, which is faith in Allah, affirming His Oneness, obeying Him and obeying His Messenger; and those who forbid evil, which is disbelief in Him, associating others with Him in worship, and disobeying His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). The ninth: those who guard the limits of Allah by upholding them and acting upon them after knowing them. His saying the Exalted ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ refers to the people of true, complete faith, who deserve the glad tidings of the Messenger (ﷺ) of victory and support in this world, deliverance from the Fire, and entry into Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. O Allah, make us among them, O Lord of the worlds.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the grace and favours of Allah the Exalted upon His servants who believe, in that He bestowed upon them their souls and their wealth and then purchased them from them.

2- The virtue of jihad and martyrdom in the way of Allah.

3- The believer must make himself feel that his body and wealth belong to Allah the Exalted, and that it is incumbent upon him to care for and protect them, until the banner of jihad is raised and the leader of the Muslims demands life and wealth, whereupon he offers his self and wealth, since they are a trust from Allah the Exalted with him.

4- The believer must not bring harm upon his soul or his wealth, since both belong to Allah the Exalted.

5- The believer must examine himself to see whether he is characterised by these nine attributes or not. If he sees a deficiency, he should complete it; if he sees perfection, he should praise Allah for it, guard it and preserve it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 113–116:

Explanation of the words:

"That they should ask forgiveness for the polytheists": that is, that they should ask Allah, exalted is He, to forgive them.

"Relatives of near kin" (ulī qurbā): people of kinship, such as fathers, sons and brothers.

"A promise" (maw'idah): that is, a promise he made to him.

"Disassociated himself from him": that is, he said, "I am free of you."

"Awwah, forbearing": the awwah is one who frequently supplicates and complains to Allah, exalted is He; and the ḥalīm is one who does not become angry and does not take to account for sin.

"What they fear" (mā yattaqūn): that is, what they fear of Allah, exalted is He, in it, so that they do not do it or so that they do not leave it.

"Any protector" (walī): the walī is one who takes charge of your affairs, protecting you and helping you.

Meaning of the verses:

When Abu Talib died upon polytheism, after the Messenger had offered him the word of tawhid (lā ilāha illā Allāh), and he refused to say it and said, "I am upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib," the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "I will certainly ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so." Some of the believers also asked forgiveness for their relatives who had died upon polytheism. Allah, exalted is He, then revealed His words: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were near of kin, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, since they had died upon polytheism, and whoever dies upon polytheism, Allah, exalted is He, has decreed that he is in the Fire. That is, it is not valid nor proper for the Prophet ﷺ and those who believe to ask forgiveness; that is, their asking forgiveness is neither valid nor proper.

When some said that Abraham had asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, Allah, exalted is He, answered: ﴿And the request for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾, and that promise was his saying: ﴿I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord; indeed, He is ever gracious to me﴾ [Maryam: 47]. But when it became clear to him that his father was an enemy of Allah, that is, that he had died upon polytheism, he disassociated himself from him and did not ask forgiveness for him. His words ﴿Indeed, Abraham was awwah and forbearing﴾ are a reason for Abraham's promising his father to ask forgiveness for him, because Abraham was one who frequently supplicated, humbled himself, grieved and lamented; therefore he promised his father to ask forgiveness for him. His words, exalted is He, ﴿And Allah would not leave a people astray after He has guided them until He has made clear to them what they should fear﴾: this verse was revealed in response to the questions of those who said, regretfully, "Indeed, we had asked forgiveness for our polytheist relatives," and so they feared. Allah, exalted is He, informed them that it is not part of His way to lead a people astray after He has guided them to the straight path until He has made clear to them what they should fear, and you asked forgiveness for your relatives before it was made clear to you that it is forbidden. However, when Allah wills to lead a people astray, He makes clear to them what they must fear in it, and if they do not fear it, He leads them astray. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 117–119:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Muhajirin (the Emigrants): those who left their homes in Makkah and elsewhere and joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah.

Al-Ansar (the Helpers): the inhabitants of Madinah from the Aws and the Khazraj, who believed and supported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Sa'at al-'usrah (the hour of hardship): the days of the march to Tabuk, marked by intense heat, hunger and thirst.

Yazigh qulub (their hearts nearly swerved): that is, they were about to incline away from the truth because of the severity of the situation and the difficulty of the moment.

Al-thalathah alladhina khullifu (the three who were left behind): Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah.

Bima rahubat (despite its vastness): that is, despite its expanse and spaciousness.

An la malja'a (that there is no refuge): that is, there is no place to take refuge in or flee to.

Al-sadiqin (the truthful): in their intentions, their words and their deeds; truthfulness is the opposite of lying.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the events of the Battle of Tabuk. In these three verses there is a declaration of the honour and nobility of the Messenger ﷺ and his righteous companions from the Ansar and the Muhajirun, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet, the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, meaning He continued it (repentance) and accepted it. His words ﴿who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ mean at the time of his departure to Tabuk, in intense heat and great want. His words ﴿after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾ refer to the difficulty of the situation and the severity of the moment. They suffered from thirst for a day. As 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "One of us would slaughter his camel, squeeze its dung, drink its liquid and place some of it on his liver." Thoughts occurred to some of the people, and their hearts nearly swerved, that is, inclined away from the truth. But Allah the Exalted made them firm, so they neither said nor did anything evil. For this reason Allah the Exalted declared in these verses their honour and their elevated station, then He turned to them in forgiveness: ﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Most Merciful.﴾

His words ﴿and the three who were left behind﴾ refer to Ka'b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah. The meaning of "left behind" is that their matter was deferred regarding the decision on their repentance, since the earlier words of Allah the Exalted had come: ﴿And others are deferred until the command of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 106]. Their repentance was thus delayed for fifty days, ﴿until, when the earth was confining for them despite its vastness, and their souls confined them, and they were certain that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him﴾. They endured the severe pain of the soul caused by the boycott that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had declared against them, awaiting the judgment of Allah, because they had stayed behind from going out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Tabuk without any excuse. So when the Prophet ﷺ returned, those who had stayed behind came forward and offered excuses, and the Messenger of Allah accepted them, and Allah turned in forgiveness to the believers among them. But these three did not come forward to offer excuses, out of fear of lying; they preferred the side of truthfulness. So Allah made them taste the pain of the boycott, then turned to them in forgiveness and made them an example of truthfulness. He then called the believers to be with them, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾ That is, fear Allah by following His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and be among the truthful in your intentions, words and deeds, so that you will be with the truthful in the Hereafter: with the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and all the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Demonstration of the virtue of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

2- Demonstration of the virtue of the Battle of Hardship over other battles, "namely the Battle of Tabuk."

3- Demonstration of Allah's favour upon the believers by preserving their hearts from swerving in times of hardship.

4- Demonstration of the virtue of Ka'b ibn Malik and his two companions in their patience, truthfulness and turning to Allah the Exalted, until relief came to them and He turned to them in forgiveness, and they became an example of truthfulness.

5- The obligation of piety and truthfulness in intentions, words, states and deeds.

*yaghīz al-kuffar* (enrages the disbelievers): i.e., it afflicts them with a rage in their souls that grieves them.

*nayl* (gain): i.e., an attainment of captives, killing, or defeat of the enemy.

*ta'ifa* (a group): i.e., a small countable group.

*liyatafaqqahu fi al-din* (that they may gain understanding in the religion): i.e., that they may learn the rulings of the religion and the secrets of its laws.

*wa liyundhiru qawmahum* (and that they may warn their people): i.e., that they may warn them of the punishment of the Fire for abandoning the practice of Allah's law.

*la'allahum yahdharun* (that they may be wary): i.e., of the punishment of Allah the Exalted, through knowledge and action.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues on the effects of the events of the Battle of Tabuk, so the Exalted says ﴿It was not for the people of Medina﴾, i.e., its inhabitants from the Emigrants and the Helpers, ﴿and those around them of the Bedouins﴾, i.e., and those dwelling around Medina of the Bedouins, such as Muzayna, Juhayna, Ghifar, Ashja' and Aslam, ﴿to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾ when he went out to jihad and called for a general mobilization. His saying ﴿nor to prefer themselves over his self﴾, i.e., by seeking ease for themselves rather than the self of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His saying ﴿that﴾, i.e., the prohibition indicated by the form "it was not for the people of Medina," which is more emphatic than a prohibition by the particle (lā), because it negates the matter: this is something that should never be at all. Therefore, it is not right for them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, lest they miss this great reward. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good﴾ is a reason establishing and confirming the reward for them if they go out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and do well in companionship and deed. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿nor do they spend an expenditure﴾, i.e., in the way of Allah, which here is jihad, ﴿small or great﴾, i.e., little or much, ﴿nor do they cross a valley﴾ going toward the enemy or returning, ﴿but that it is written for them﴾, i.e., that mentioned expenditure and travel in the way of Allah. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾, i.e., a reward for the best deed they used to do before going out in the way of Allah. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Why should not a group from every division of them go forth﴾, i.e., from every tribe of them, a group, i.e., a company, ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾ through what they hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and learn from him, ﴿and warn their people﴾ of the consequences of polytheism, evil and corruption, ﴿that they may be wary﴾ of that, so that they are saved from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. This verse was revealed when the Muslims heard and saw the results of staying behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "We will never again stay behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we will not stay behind from any raid as long as we live." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse guiding them to what is better and more excellent, saying ﴿Why not﴾, i.e., why do not a group from every division of them, i.e., from every tribe or clan of theirs, go forth, and a group only remain, instead of all of them going out and leaving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone. For their going out in this order is more beneficial for them. Those who remain with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ go out with him when he goes out, gaining understanding in the religion through their companionship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the rest are also occupied with their religious and worldly affairs. When those who gained understanding return, they teach their brothers what they missed of knowledge and the secrets of the Law. Likewise, those who go forth to jihad may witness the victory of Allah for His allies and the defeat of His enemies, and they also witness the weakness of the disbelievers, the corruption of their hearts and morals, and the wretchedness of their lives. They then return to their brothers and warn them of what the people of disbelief and corruption are upon, so they beware of it and avoid it, and in this is good for all. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and that they may warn their people when they return to them, that they may be wary﴾.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation to prefer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over oneself in every good, indeed even with life itself.

2- Clarification of the virtue of going forth in the way of Allah, and the great reward therein.

3- The virtue of excellence and its people.

4- The virtue of seeking knowledge and of jihad is equal, on condition of sincere intention in both; and the seeker of knowledge does not attain this reward unless he learns in order to teach, then acts, then teaches freely for the sake of Allah; and the fighter does not attain this reward unless it is solely to raise high the word of Allah.

5- The community's need for jihad and the mujahidin is equal to its need for knowledge and the scholars, exactly alike.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verse 123:

Explanation of the words:

"Āmanū" (those who believe): i.e., in Allah and His Messenger, and in the promise of Allah and His warning.

"Alladhīna yalūnakum" (those who are near to you): i.e., who are adjacent to your lands and borders.

"Min al-kuffār" (of the disbelievers): "min" here is explicative (bayāniyya), meaning "namely the disbelievers."

"Wa-l-yajidū fīkum ghilẓah" (and let them find harshness in you): i.e., strength of might and severity of resolve, so that they fear you and are routed before you.

"Ma'a al-muttaqīn" (with those who are God-conscious): i.e., with His help and support. The muttaqūn (the God-conscious, those who guard themselves against wrongdoing) are those who guard against shirk, sins, and departing from the divine laws regarding victory and defeat.

Meaning of the noble verse:

When the Arabian Peninsula had been purified of shirk and became the abode of Islam, this being in the final part of the Messenger's life (ﷺ), after the Battle of Tabuk, Allah the Exalted commanded the believers to continue striving in His path after the death of their Prophet, and guided them to the method they must follow in this: that they begin by calling to and fighting the nearest disbelievers to them, meaning the disbelievers bordering their frontiers, such as those of Jordan, Syria, or Iraq for example. They are to encamp near them and invite them to one of three things: entering the religion of Allah, Islam; or accepting the protection of the Muslims by entering their lands and paying the jizya upon those among them who are able, in exchange for their protection, their instruction, and their governance with justice and Islamic mercy; or fighting until Allah judges between us and you. If the land of this enemy is then joined to their lands and they acquire other borders, they shall do as they did at first, and so on, until there is no fitnah and the religion is entirely for Allah, so that mankind may be happy in this world and the next. And He commanded them to know that Allah has not charged them with jihad except that He is with them and their helper, but on the condition that they fear Him in His commands and prohibitions. This is what the noble verse indicates: ﴿O you who believe, fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you, and let them find in you harshness﴾, i.e., strength of might and severity of resolve in war, ﴿and know that Allah is with the God-conscious﴾, i.e., with His help and support.

Guidance from the noble verse:

From the guidance of the noble verse:

1- The obligation of jihad and its continuation until no fitnah, no shirk, and no oppression of a believer remains, and both religion and rule belong entirely to Allah the Exalted.

2- The legitimacy of beginning jihad with the disbelievers nearest to the lands of the Muslims, by the principle (the nearer are more entitled to the good).

3- When the lands of Islam expand, it becomes incumbent upon the people of each region to fight those who are nearest to them, in order of proximity.

4- Allah's promise of victory and support to those who are God-conscious, both in general and in particular.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 9, verses 124–127:

Explanation of the words:

Surah: a portion of the Qur'an, whether it is a group of verses from a surah or a complete surah on its own.

"It has increased him in faith" (zādathu īmānan): meaning the surah strengthened his faith and increased it, because it is like beneficial rain.

"Rejoice" (yastabshirūn): rejoicing in God's favour upon them.

"In their hearts is a sickness" (fī qulūbihim maraḍ): meaning doubt, hypocrisy and polytheism.

"It has added to them filth" (fa-zādathum rijsan): meaning impurity added to the impurity of their hearts and souls.

"Are tested" (yuftanūn): meaning are tried.

"Nor do they remember" (wa-lā hum yadhakkarūn): meaning they do not take heed, because their hearts are dead.

"God has turned their hearts away" (ṣaraf Allāh qulūbahum): a supplication against them, that they not return to the truth after turning away from it.

"They do not understand" (lā yafqahūn): meaning they do not grasp the secrets of the discourse, because of the darkness of their hearts and the corruption of their souls.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the last discussion of the hypocrites in Surat Barā'a (al-Tawba), the surah that exposes the hypocrites. God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down﴾, meaning of the surahs of the Qur'an, which have reached 114 surahs, revealed and recited while they were absent from the gathering in which it was recited. Among them, that is among the hypocrites, is one who says: ﴿Which of you has had its faith increased by this?﴾ Their saying this is mockery and disdain from them. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who believe﴾ truly and sincerely, ﴿it has increased them in faith﴾, because it was revealed with rulings or reports that were not known to them, so they believed in them when they were revealed, and thereby their faith increased and grew, just as their faith grows until it becomes certainty regarding the verses that descend. His saying ﴿and they rejoice﴾ means they are glad and pleased with the news that was revealed, and the whole Qur'an is good, just as they are also rejoicing in their faith and the increase of their certainty. ﴿As for those in whose hearts is a sickness﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it has added to them filth﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿to their filth; and they died while they were disbelievers﴾.

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾ meaning: do these sick ones of hypocrisy persist in their hypocrisy and not see that they are tested, that is, because of their hypocrisy, once or twice, meaning they are examined through obligations, disgrace and other things. ﴿Then they do not repent﴾ from their hypocrisy, ﴿nor do they take heed﴾, so that they would be admonished and repent. This is what the first verses [124], second [125] and third [126] indicate. As for the fourth verse [127], it includes the evil state of these hypocrites and the ugliness of their conduct, so it recorded upon them a stain of shame and disgrace until the Day of Resurrection, when God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down﴾, meaning while they are in the gathering and it is recited to those sitting, and they are among them. ﴿They look at one another﴾ and say secretly and furtively: let us get up from this gathering in which we are being reproached and insulted. ﴿Does anyone see you?﴾ meaning from among the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). If the answer is: no one sees us, they slip away furtively. God, exalted is He, said in supplication against them: ﴿God has turned their hearts away﴾, meaning from guidance, ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾, meaning they do not grasp the secrets of the verses and what they guide to. Their conduct is caused by their poor understanding, and the cause of their poor understanding is the darkness of their hearts, and the cause of that darkness is doubt, polytheism and hypocrisy, and we seek refuge in God, exalted is He.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Establishing the principle that faith increases and decreases: it increases through obedience and decreases through disobedience.

2- Permissibility of rejoicing in faith and righteous deeds.

3- The one whose heart is sick increases in sickness, and the one whose heart is sound increases in soundness; this is a sunnah of God among His servants.

4- Uncovering the hidden states of the hypocrites and exposing them in the last verse of Surat al-Tawba that speaks of them.

5- It is recommended not to say "we have finished the prayer or the lesson" (inṣarafnā) but to say "the prayer has concluded" (inqaḍat al-ṣalāt) or "the lesson has concluded" (inqaḍa al-dars), and the like.

Explanation of the Words:

Rasulun min anfusikum (a messenger from among yourselves): That is, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ﷺ, of your own kind, an Arab.

Aziz alayhi (grievous to him): That is, difficult and hard.

Ma ataum (what distresses you): That is, what is hard on you and difficult for you to bear.

Harisun alaykum (eager over you): That is, eager for your guidance and for what is good for you and your happiness.

Ra'uf (kind): Compassionate.

Rahim (merciful): Tender, inclined to kindness and mercy.

Fa in tawallaw (but if they turn away): That is, they turn away from the religion of Allah and from the guidance you have brought.

Hasbiyal-Lah (Allah is sufficient for me): That is, Allah is my sufficiency.

La ilaha illa Huwa (there is no god but He): That is, there is no one worthy of worship except Him.

Tawakkaltu (I have placed my trust): That is, I have entrusted my affair to Him and relied upon Him.

Rabbul-'arshil-'azim (Lord of the Mighty Throne): The Throne of Allah, the Exalted; none is greater than it except its Creator, Mighty and Majestic, since His Footstool encompasses the heavens and the earth, and the proportion of the Footstool to the Throne is like a ring thrown onto a desert plain.

The Meaning of the Two Noble Verses:

At the close of Surah at-Tawbah, Allah the Exalted says to all the Arabs: ﴿Indeed, there has come to you a messenger﴾, that is, a noble, great one, ﴿from among yourselves﴾, an 'Adnani, Qurashi, Hashimi, Muttalibi, whose lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness you know. ﴿It grieves him what you suffer﴾, that is, what is hard on you distresses him and what pains you pains him, because he is one of you, advising you as a kinsman advises his people. ﴿He is eager over you﴾, that is, for your guidance, your perfection and your happiness. ﴿For the believers﴾, from among you and from among other people in general, ﴿he is kind and merciful﴾, that is, tender and compassionate, loving their mercy and bringing good to them. So believe in him, follow the light he has brought, and you will be guided and made happy, and you will not disbelieve and go astray and be wretched. And His saying, ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, they turn away from your call, then do not grieve, and say: ﴿Allah is sufficient for me﴾, that is, my Lord suffices me in everything that concerns me. ﴿There is no god but He﴾, that is, there is no one worthy of worship besides Him; therefore I worship Him and call to His worship. ﴿In Him I have placed my trust﴾, that is, in all my affairs. ﴿And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾: whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be, and He is capable of all things.

Guidance from the Two Verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's favour upon the Arabs in particular and upon mankind in general in sending Muhammad ﷺ, the seal of His prophets.

2- Explanation of the perfection of his ﷺ character.

3- The obligation of trusting in Allah and relying upon Him in everything the servant undertakes.

4- The greatness of the Throne of the Most Merciful, Exalted is He.
